plonk-pk-structure.details:
## Conventions
n = `domain0.Cardinality` = `ecc.NextPowerOfTwo(nbConstraints + len(spr.Public))` (setup.go:271-275 `initFFTDomain`, prove.go:234-236; power-of-two rounding in `createDomain`, domain.go:176-177). bn254 `fr.Element` = 32 bytes / 4 limbs; `G1Affine` = 64 bytes in memory (2 fp). `offset` = nbPublic + nbConstraints (≤ n; the unpadded region).

## 1. ProvingKey contents (bn254)

`type ProvingKey struct` — /home/work/repositories/gnark/backend/plonk/bn254/setup.go:88-93:
- `Kzg kzg.ProvingKey` — canonical (monomial-basis) SRS, `G1 []bn254.G1Affine` (kzg.go:37-39). Sliced to exactly **n+3** points at setup.go:126 (`srs.Pk.G1[:int(vk.Size)+3]`; the +3 covers KZG opening of blinded polynomials of length n+3; size check setup.go:109).
- `KzgLagrange kzg.ProvingKey` — Lagrange-basis SRS over the small domain, exactly **n** points (setup.go:127; strict equality check setup.go:114).
- `Vk *VerifyingKey` — embedded verifying key, needed by Prove (setup.go:92).

That is the ENTIRE pk. **Everything in it is static across proofs** — the prover never writes to pk.Kzg, pk.KzgLagrange, or pk.Vk. Canonical vs Lagrange: Kzg.G1 = [G, αG, α²G, …] (monomial); KzgLagrange.G1 = commitments to the Lagrange basis polys L_i over the small domain. Both are pure MSM bases.

**Crucially, the Trace and FFT domains are NOT in the pk on this branch** (unlike older gnark releases). They are rebuilt from the SparseR1CS inside `newInstance` at every `Prove` call:
- domain0 = `fft.NewDomain(sizeSystem)` — prove.go:236 (with twiddle precompute, no cache).
- domain1 = `fft.NewDomain(4*sizeSystem, fft.WithoutPrecompute())` — prove.go:247-251 (8× if sizeSystem<6).
- `s.trace = NewTrace(spr, s.domain0)` — prove.go:254.

### Trace contents (`type Trace`, setup.go:67-85), all sizes per circuit:
- `Ql, Qr, Qm, Qo, Qk *iop.Polynomial` — each n fr.Elements, built **Lagrange/Regular** (setup.go:204-210). First nbPublic entries are placeholders: Ql[i]=-1, others 0; Qk public slots left 0 to be completed by prover (setup.go:184-190).
- `Qcp []*iop.Polynomial` — one per BSB22 commitment, each n fr.Elements, Lagrange/Regular, 1 at committed wire positions (setup.go:211-219).
- `S1, S2, S3 *iop.Polynomial` — each n fr.Elements, **Lagrange/Regular** (despite local variable names `s1Canonical`, the Form is `{Basis: Lagrange, Layout: Regular}`, setup.go:367-371).
- `S []int64` — the full permutation, **3n entries** (24n bytes) (setup.go:289-343).

### Basis lifecycle inside one proof (load-bearing for any device-resident design)
`s.x[id_Ql] = s.trace.Ql` etc. at prove.go:559-565 are **pointer aliases**, not copies. During `computeNumerator` (prove.go:841-1123) every poly in `s.x` is cycled rho=4 times: `ToCanonical(domain0)` → scale by coset/twiddle vector → `ToLagrange(domain0).ToRegular()` (prove.go:1035-1057), evaluated via the `allConstraints` closure, then a final cleanup converts all of them to **Canonical/Regular** and rescales (`scalePowers` by the inverse accumulated shift) (prove.go:1090-1114). After that:
- `innerComputeLinearizedPoly` reads trace.Ql/Qr/Qm/Qo coefficients as canonical (prove.go:1433-1437), trace.S3 canonical (prove.go:1418), and converts trace.Qk Lagrange→Canonical in place at prove.go:1420 (trace.Qk was never aliased into s.x — `completeQk` works on a Clone, prove.go:352).
- `batchOpening` opens trace.S1/S2 coefficients as canonical (prove.go:813-814).
So the trace is destructively transformed every proof; the next proof rebuilds it from spr. (Note: the in-code comment at prove.go:1030-1034 explicitly flags that the rho*2 FFTs of the static pk polynomials could be precomputed at "huge memory footprint" cost — i.e., exactly the GPU pinning opportunity.)

### Memory inventory (host) per circuit
- pk.Kzg.G1: (n+3)·64 B; pk.KzgLagrange.G1: n·64 B.
- trace: (5 + #Qcp)·n·32 B selectors + 3·n·32 B (S1..S3) + 3n·8 B (S int64).
- domain0 precompute: twiddles + twiddlesInv ≈ 2·(n/2+1 + n/4+1 + …) ≈ 2n elements, cosetTable + cosetTableInv = 2n elements ⇒ ≈ 4n·32 B (domain.go:244-275).
- prover transient: cres 4n, buf n, blindedZ n+3, linearizedPolynomial n+3, h 3(n+2) shards inside a 4n coefficient vector.

## 2. fft.Domain (gnark-crypto v0.20.1, ecc/bn254/fr/fft/domain.go:27-55)

```go
type Domain struct {
    Cardinality            uint64
    CardinalityInv         fr.Element
    Generator              fr.Element   // ω, primitive Cardinality-th root of unity (fr.Generator(m), domain.go:204)
    GeneratorInv           fr.Element
    FrMultiplicativeGen    fr.Element   // coset shift u; default 5 for bn254 (GeneratorFullMultiplicativeGroup, domain.go:58-64)
    FrMultiplicativeGenInv fr.Element
    withPrecompute bool                 // false ⇒ twiddles computed on the fly
    twiddles      [][]fr.Element        // per FFT stage; stage0 = 1+n/2 powers of ω, stage i strided (domain.go:277-298)
    twiddlesInv   [][]fr.Element
    cosetTable    []fr.Element          // <1,u,u²,…,uⁿ⁻¹>, length n
    cosetTableInv []fr.Element
}
```
Accessors `Twiddles()/TwiddlesInv()/CosetTable()/CosetTableInv()` (domain.go:210-242) return an **error** if the domain was created `WithoutPrecompute()`. Defaults (options.go `domainOptions`): withPrecompute=true, withCache=false. NewDomain has an optional weak-pointer cache (domain.go:88-172), only active with `WithCache()` — the plonk prover does NOT use it, so domain0's ~4n-element precompute is redone every Prove.

**Small domain (domain0)**: cardinality n; coset shift u=5; used for all per-poly FFTs in computeNumerator, the L1/Lagrange computations, `BuildRatioCopyConstraint`, and `ToCanonical` scale-back. `vk.CosetShift = domain.FrMultiplicativeGen` (setup.go:120); `vk.Generator`, `vk.Size`, `vk.SizeInv` from the same domain (setup.go:121-123).

**Big domain (domain1)**: cardinality 4n (8n when sizeSystem<6, prove.go:247-251), created WithoutPrecompute ⇒ only the six scalar fields are valid. The prover reads domain1.FrMultiplicativeGen (prove.go:889, 938, 1334), domain1.Generator (prove.go:1021, 1337), domain1.Cardinality (rho = 4 at prove.go:936, result vector size prove.go:949, bit-reverse width prove.go:990), and runs exactly one big inverse-FFT: `a.ToCanonical(bigDomain)` in `divideByZH` (prove.go:1320) over 4n elements with on-the-fly twiddles. Rationale: quotient h has degree 3(n+1)+2 ⇒ lives in 3(n+2) dims ⇒ 4n is the next convenient power-of-two multiple (comment prove.go:244-246). Both domains share the same coset generator u=5; the rho cosets of the big domain are enumerated by shifting with `domain1.FrMultiplicativeGen` once then `domain1.Generator` (prove.go:937-940).

For ICICLE: groth16 initializes the device NTT domain with `fft.Generator(2*pk.Domain.Cardinality)` (icicle/groth16/bn254/icicle.go:96) and tracks a per-device max domain size (icicle.go:134-168 `nttDomainMaxByDevice`). A plonk port must init for ≥ 4n (the big-domain inverse FFT), and needs the coset generators (the `CosetGenerator [fr.Limbs*2]uint32` field in deviceInfo, provingkey.go:19, fed to coset NTT configs).

## 3. Per-proof pk reads (device-upload candidates)

pk.KzgLagrange.G1 (Lagrange MSM base, length n):
- L commit: MSM over `KzgLagrange.G1[:offset]` (prove.go:438); R, O: `[nbPublic:offset]` (prove.go:457, 476) — the s0-subtraction trick (comment prove.go:387-403) shrinks MSM length to the unpadded region and adds `s0·Kzg.G1[0]` (prove.go:427).
- Z commit: `kzg.Commit(z, pk.KzgLagrange)` length n (prove.go:532 via commitToPolyAndBlinding, called prove.go:662).
- BSB22 commitments: `kzg.Commit(..., pk.KzgLagrange)` length n each (prove.go:300).

pk.Kzg.G1 (canonical MSM base, length n+3):
- blinding-factor commits: MSMs over `Kzg.G1[:np]` and the non-contiguous window `Kzg.G1[n:n+np]`, np ≤ 3 (commitBlindingFactor, prove.go:1223-1236; called prove.go:445,464,483,536).
- quotient shards h1,h2,h3: 3 commits of length n+2 (n+3 with StatisticalZK) (prove.go:615 → commitToQuotient prove.go:1263-1282; shard slicing prove.go:689-724).
- linearized polynomial commit, length n+3 (prove.go:788).
- ZShiftedOpening: `kzg.Open(blindedZ, ζω, pk.Kzg)` ⇒ one commit of length n+3 (prove.go:681; kzg.go:181-205).
- batch opening: `kzg.BatchOpenSinglePoint(..., pk.Kzg, ...)` ⇒ one commit of the folded poly, length n+3 (prove.go:827-834; kzg.go:311-338) + 6+#Qcp Horner evals.

pk.Vk (tiny, O(1)): Generator (prove.go:678), CosetShift (prove.go:1393-1394), S[0..2]/Ql..Qk/Qcp digests for Fiat-Shamir binding (prove.go:498 → bindPublicData verify.go:315-359) and as digestsToOpen (prove.go:816-824).

**One-time upload candidates (PinToGPU analog):** pk.Kzg.G1 and pk.KzgLagrange.G1 — immutable, used in every proof, together (2n+3)·64 B ≈ 128 MB at n=2²⁰. Secondary candidates are the per-circuit trace data (Ql,Qr,Qm,Qo,Qk,Qcp evaluations; S1,S2,S3; permutation S; optionally their precomputed coset-FFT forms per the prove.go:1030 comment) and domain twiddles — but these are NOT in the pk today; they're rebuilt+mutated per proof, so pinning them requires new per-circuit caching keyed off the wrapper pk (and pristine copies, since the CPU path destroys them). The prover additionally needs spr for `NewTrace` (prove.go:254) and `spr.Solve` (prove.go:320) every proof.

Groth16 reference machinery to mirror: `setupDevicePointers` guarded by `setupMu` with idempotence via `pk.deviceInfo != nil` (icicle.go:88-95); PinToGPU branch uploads each base via `loadG1` (CopyToDevice + `AffineFromMontgomery` conversion on device, icicle.go:319-331) or `loadG1Raw` (Montgomery preserved, MSM config `AreBasesMontgomeryForm=true`, icicle.go:333-344); `FreeGPUResources` (icicle.go:1493); per-device exclusive prove mutex `getDeviceProveMutex` (icicle.go:77-86) and NTT-domain max tracking (icicle.go:53-60, 134-168); `pk.PinToGPU = cfg.PinToGPU` set at Prove entry (icicle.go:792).

## 4. Serialization

Native pk stream (`(pk *ProvingKey).writeTo`, marshal.go:96-129): **[vk stream][pk.Kzg.G1][pk.KzgLagrange.G1]**, each via the curve encoder (slice lengths as uint32; compressed points 32 B by default, raw 64 B via WriteRawTo). `readFrom` (marshal.go:141-165) allocates `pk.Vk = &VerifyingKey{}` fresh (marshal.go:142); `UnsafeReadFrom` skips subgroup checks (marshal.go:137-139 → kzg/marshal.go:152-159).

vk stream (marshal.go:177-212), versioned: keyVersionMarker (uint64 0), version (uint64 1), Size, SizeInv, Generator, NbPublicVariables, CosetShift, S[0],S[1],S[2], Ql,Qr,Qm,Qo,Qk, Qcp (slice of digests), Kzg.G1, Kzg.G2[0], Kzg.G2[1], Kzg.Lines (2×2×66 line evals × 2 fp each ≈ 17 KB), CommitmentConstraintIndexes. ReadFrom handles the legacy unversioned layout when the first word ≠ 0 (marshal.go:229-306). `vk.version = currentKeyVersion` is set inside writeTo (marshal.go:179).

**Wrapping pattern (groth16 reference, provingkey.go:18-42):** `type ProvingKey struct { groth16_bn254.ProvingKey; *deviceInfo; setupMu sync.Mutex; PinToGPU bool }`. Because the native pk is embedded **by value**, all pointer-receiver methods (WriteTo, WriteRawTo, ReadFrom, UnsafeReadFrom, IsDifferent, and for plonk `VerifyingKey()` at setup.go:162-164 and `Version()` at setup.go:157-159) are promoted onto `*icicle.ProvingKey`. Consequences, confirmed by `backend/accelerated/icicle/groth16/marshal_test.go` (round-trips native→icicle and icicle→native and proves with both):
- The serialized bytes are **exactly** the native format; device fields (`*deviceInfo`, mutex, bool) are never serialized.
- The wrapper automatically satisfies the generic `plonk.ProvingKey` interface (plonk.go:59-70: WriterTo, ReaderFrom, WriterRawTo, UnsafeReaderFrom, VerifyingKey()).
- After ReadFrom, deviceInfo is nil ⇒ lazy `setupDevicePointers` on first Prove, as in groth16 (icicle.go:797-803).
So: **no serialization implications** — the pattern transfers verbatim. One structural difference: `plonk_bn254.Setup` returns `(*ProvingKey, *VerifyingKey, error)` (setup.go:95) instead of groth16's fill-in-place `Setup(r1cs, &pk.ProvingKey, &vk)` (groth16_icicle.go:109). The icicle plonk Setup wrapper should copy the returned value: `pk.ProvingKey = *nativePk` — cheap (two slice headers + one pointer; shares the underlying G1 arrays, and `pk.Vk` pointer stays equal to the returned vk).

## 5. Trace / permutation construction (setup side) and prover re-reads

`buildPermutation` (setup.go:289-343): builds `S` of length 3n by chaining, per wire id, the positions where that wire appears in the concatenated L‖R‖O index table (lro filled from c.XA/XB/XC per constraint, setup.go:310-317), forming maximal cycles. `computePermutationPolynomials` (setup.go:348-373): evaluates the identity support `<g> ‖ u<g> ‖ u²<g>` (getSupportPermutation, setup.go:377-392, 3n elements) at the permuted indices to produce S1,S2,S3 evaluation vectors (Lagrange/Regular). Setup commits S1,S2,S3 → vk.S[0..2] and Ql..Qk,Qcp → vk digests using **pk.KzgLagrange** (commitTrace, setup.go:235-269; the "expressed in canonical basis afterwards" comment at setup.go:136-138 is stale — polynomials stay Lagrange and are committed against the Lagrange SRS).

Prover re-reads per proof: (a) `trace.S` (the int64 permutation) in `iop.BuildRatioCopyConstraint` (prove.go:645-656) which internally re-derives the 3n-element identity support and does a batch inversion (ratios.go:138-220) — Z comes out Lagrange; (b) `trace.S1/S2` evaluated at ζ (prove.go:1382-1388) and their canonical coefficients opened in the batch proof (prove.go:813-814); (c) `trace.S3` canonical coefficients in the linearization (prove.go:1418, 1443-1445); (d) selectors as described in §1. Nothing else from setup's permutation machinery is needed at prove time.

## 6. VerifyingKey / verifier

vk fields (setup.go:41-64): Size, SizeInv, Generator, NbPublicVariables, kzg.VerifyingKey (G2[2], G1, 66 precomputed pairing Lines), CosetShift, S[3] digests, Ql/Qr/Qm/Qo/Qk digests, Qcp []digest, CommitmentConstraintIndexes, version. vk is written first inside the pk stream and pk.Vk == the vk returned by Setup (setup.go:99).

`Verify(proof *Proof, vk *VerifyingKey, publicWitness fr.Vector, ...)` (verify.go:34) touches only proof + vk + public witness: subgroup checks on all proof points (verify.go:52-75), Fiat-Shamir replay via the same `bindPublicData`/`deriveRandomness` the prover uses (verify.go:83-112, 315-383), PI evaluation, linearized-digest reconstruction from vk digests (verify.go:255-280), `kzg.FoldProof` + pairing check with vk.Kzg (verify.go:307). The generic `plonk.Verify` dispatches on the **proof's** concrete type (plonk.go:140-169). Therefore: if the ICICLE prover returns a `*plonk_bn254.Proof` produced under the identical transcript ordering (gamma ← vk digests + public inputs + LRO; beta; alpha ← Bsb22 + Z; zeta ← H[0..2]) and identical polynomial/blinding structure, the verifier path requires **zero changes**. Note proofs cannot be byte-identical across runs even on CPU (blinding polynomials use SetRandom, prove.go:1239-1253; quotient randomizers prove.go:239-242) — the correct acceptance criterion is "verifies under the unmodified verifier", optionally plus a determinism test with stubbed randomness.

## Proof struct (for completeness, prove.go:78-96 / marshal.go:28-84)
LRO[3], Z, H[3] (kzg.Digest each), Bsb22Commitments []Digest, BatchedProof {H, ClaimedValues[6+#Qcp]}, ZShiftedOpening {H, ClaimedValue}. Encoded in that order.
gotchas: The Plonk ProvingKey on this branch is SLIM (setup.go:88-93): unlike groth16 (and older gnark plonk), it contains no Trace, no domains, no permutation — those are rebuilt from the SparseR1CS inside every Prove (prove.go:236-254). A GPU 'pin trace to device' feature therefore cannot just read pk fields like groth16's setupDevicePointers does (it reads pk.Domain.Cardinality, icicle.go:96); it must derive n from vk.Size or spr and build/cache the trace itself.

Trace polynomials are destructively mutated during each proof: s.x[id_Ql..id_S3] alias the trace's *iop.Polynomial pointers (prove.go:559-565), and computeNumerator converts them through 4 coset rounds ending Canonical/Regular with a scalePowers rescale (prove.go:1035-1057, 1090-1114). Any device-resident static copy must be taken from a pristine per-circuit snapshot, and downstream consumers (linearization prove.go:1433-1437, batch opening prove.go:813-814) expect the CANONICAL form, not the Lagrange form NewTrace produces.

trace.Qk is special: never aliased into s.x (completeQk clones it, prove.go:352), stays Lagrange until innerComputeLinearizedPoly converts it in place at prove.go:1420; its public-input slots remain ZERO (incomplete Qk) in the linearization — public inputs enter via the verifier's PI term. Do not 'fix' this on device.

pk.Kzg.G1 has exactly n+3 points (setup.go:126), not the full SRS; commitBlindingFactor reads a NON-CONTIGUOUS window Kzg.G1[n:n+np] (prove.go:1233), and the L/R/O MSMs use variable sub-slices KzgLagrange.G1[:offset] / [nbPublic:offset] with in-place witness mutation before/after (prove.go:434-487) — device MSM wrappers must support offset/length sub-views.

domain1 (big domain, 4n; 8n when sizeSystem<6, prove.go:247-251) is created WithoutPrecompute: Twiddles()/CosetTable() return errors (domain.go:210-242). Only its 6 scalar fields are valid. domain0 is created with default options each Prove — withCache=false, so ~4n field elements of twiddles/coset tables are recomputed per proof on CPU.

ICICLE NTT device domain must be initialized for the BIG domain size (4n) — groth16 uses fft.Generator(2*cardinality) (icicle.go:96); reusing that verbatim under-sizes the plonk domain. Per-device NTT-domain max tracking and the per-device exclusive prove mutex (icicle.go:53-86, 134-168) are package-level state in the groth16 icicle package; a plonk icicle package coexisting on the same GPU must share or replicate this to avoid ReleaseDomain/InitDomain races.

Serialization: the wrapper must add NO methods that shadow WriteTo/ReadFrom — promotion from the embedded native pk gives byte-identical streams (verified by groth16 marshal_test.go pattern). ReadFrom reallocates pk.Vk (marshal.go:142), so never cache pointers into the old Vk in deviceInfo. plonk_bn254.ProvingKey has no IsDifferent helper (groth16's is at backend/groth16/bn254/setup.go:616) — port one or compare serialized bytes in tests.

plonk_bn254.Setup RETURNS a new *ProvingKey (setup.go:95) instead of groth16's fill-by-pointer Setup; the icicle Setup wrapper must copy the struct value into the embedded field (pk.ProvingKey = *nativePk) — safe and cheap (slice headers + Vk pointer are shared).

Proofs are randomized (blinding polys SetRandom prove.go:1239-1253; StatisticalZK randomizers prove.go:239-242): byte-identical proofs across CPU/GPU runs are impossible. Correctness criterion = unmodified plonk_bn254.Verify accepts; also note plonk.Verify dispatches on the concrete proof type (plonk.go:140-169), so the GPU prover must return *plonk_bn254.Proof.

Fiat-Shamir ordering is load-bearing and partially concurrent: gamma binds vk.S[0..2], Ql..Qk, Qcp digests + public inputs + LRO commitments (verify.go:315-359, prove.go:498-521); alpha binds Bsb22Commitments then Z (prove.go:542-550); zeta binds H[0..2] (prove.go:552-555). Any GPU pipeline reordering must preserve commit-before-challenge dependencies enforced today by the channel graph (chLRO/chZ/chH/...).

StatisticalZK option changes quotient shard lengths: h1,h2 = n+3 and h3 = n+2 with randomizer stitching (prove.go:689-724) vs n+2 each without — MSM sizes differ by option, and linearization loops branch on it (prove.go:1466-1482).

kzg.Commit rejects len(p) > len(pk.G1) (kzg.go:162); Lagrange commits pass length-n vectors against the length-n Lagrange key — padding vectors to n+3 on device would break the host-side equivalence checks if mirrored back.

Montgomery-form discipline from groth16 icicle: G1 bases uploaded via loadG1 are converted OUT of Montgomery on device (icicle.go:319-331), scalars converted via FromMontgomery after copy (icicle.go:121); loadG1Raw keeps Montgomery and sets AreBasesMontgomeryForm=true in MSM config (icicle.go:333-344). Pick one convention per buffer and keep it consistent for pinned KZG bases.

The stale comment at setup.go:135-138 claims trace polys are 'expressed in canonical basis afterwards' — they are not; commitTrace commits Lagrange evaluations against the Lagrange SRS (setup.go:235-269). Don't design device layouts off that comment.

fr.Generator(m) / 2-adicity limits: domain of size 4n must exist (bn254 2-adicity 28 — fine for n up to 2^26); bw6-761 fr has lower 2-adicity (check before porting), and bw6-761 points are 96-byte fp coordinates (3x bn254 memory per point).
open_questions: Where to cache the per-circuit device-resident trace/selector data given the trace is rebuilt per Prove: inside the wrapper ProvingKey's deviceInfo keyed by nothing (one circuit per pk, matching groth16's assumption), or keyed by the spr pointer to guard against the same pk being used with a different ccs?

Scope for phase 1: accelerate only the ~9 MSMs per proof (sizes between offset and n+3) while keeping CPU FFTs, vs also porting the computeNumerator coset-evaluation pipeline (4 rounds x ~13 small NTTs + pointwise constraint evaluation) which is the other dominant cost and would let selector/permutation cosets be precomputed on device per the prove.go:1030-1034 comment.

BuildRatioCopyConstraint (grand product Z) recomputes a 3n identity support + batch inversion per proof on CPU (ratios.go:155-220) — candidate for device, but it consumes the int64 permutation S; decide host/device split.

The icicle-gnark v3.2.2 wrapper exposes NTT with coset support per curve — confirm the exact CosetGen config semantics match gnark's u=5 shift and the bit-reverse ordering conventions used in computeNumerator (LagrangeCoset/BitReverse result, prove.go:1119) before replacing divideByZH's big inverse FFT.

## 2. How plonk tests construct circuits + SRS (recipe)

Canonical pattern, from backend/plonk/plonk_test.go:
- **Compile**: `ccs, err := frontend.Compile(curve.ScalarField(), scs.NewBuilder, &circuit)` (line 324; scs = sparse R1CS builder, mandatory for plonk).
- **SRS**: `srs, srsLagrange, err := unsafekzg.NewSRS(ccs)` (line 78, mem-cache) or `unsafekzg.NewSRS(ccs, unsafekzg.WithFSCache())` (line 339, persists to `~/.gnark/kzg`, file name `kzgsrs-<curve>-<size>`; options.go:82-92). NewSRS returns `(canonical kzg.SRS, lagrange kzg.SRS)`; sizing at kzgsrs.go:54-58: `sizeLagrange = ecc.NextPowerOfTwo(nbConstraints + ccs.GetNbPublicVariables())`, `sizeCanonical = sizeLagrange + 3`.
- **Setup**: `pk, vk, err := plonk.Setup(ccs, srs, srsLagrange)` (plonk.go:94). Setup validates: `len(srs.Pk.G1) >= domain.Cardinality+3` and `len(srsLagrange.Pk.G1) == domain.Cardinality` (bn254/setup.go:108-117) where `domain.Cardinality = NextPowerOfTwo(nbConstraints + len(spr.Public))` (setup.go:273).
- **Witness**: `fullWitness, _ := frontend.NewWitness(_solution, curve.ScalarField())`; `publicWitness, _ := fullWitness.Public()`.
- **Prove/Verify**: `proof, _ := plonk.Prove(ccs, pk, fullWitness)` (plonk.go:117); `plonk.Verify(proof, vk, publicWitness)` (plonk.go:138).
- **PK-immutability check** (TestProver lines 43-54): `pk.WriteTo(&b1)` before Prove, `pk.WriteTo(&b2)` after, `bytes.Equal` — "plonk prover mutated the proving key". A GPU plonk test should replicate this; it constrains the GPU prover to not mutate host-side PK state.
- **Negative check** (lines 60-64): verifying with the full witness must error containing "witness length is invalid".
- **Curve set**: `getCurves()` (line 377-382): `testing.Short()` → `{BN254}` else `gnark.Curves()` = `{BN254, BLS12_377, BLS12_381, BW6_761}` (doc.go:25-32) — exactly the project's 4 target curves.
- Subtests use either raw `t.Run(curve.String(), ...)` + `require.New(t)` (TestProver) or `assert := test.NewAssert(t)` + `assert.Run(func(assert *test.Assert){...}, curve.String())` (TestCustomHashToField etc.).

`test.Assert.CheckCircuit` (assert_checkcircuit.go:35) is the registry-driven alternative: its `_plonk` tBackend (lines 316-334) does unsafekzg.NewSRS → plonk.Setup → plonk.Prove → plonk.Verify; backends are hardwired to `backend.GROTH16`/`backend.PLONK` (switch at lines 109-116 panics otherwise), and prove/verify only run under `-tags=prover_checks` or `release_checks` (profile selection assert_options.go:41-49, profiles in assert_profile.go:30-49). **GPU correctness test recipe** (the Phase-3/5 hard gate):
```go
//go:build icicle
// in backend/accelerated/icicle/plonk/marshal_test.go (package plonk_test)
ccs, _ := frontend.Compile(curve.ScalarField(), scs.NewBuilder, &circuit{})
srs, srsLagrange, _ := unsafekzg.NewSRS(ccs)
nativePK, vk, _ := native_plonk.Setup(ccs, srs, srsLagrange)
iciPK := icicle_plonk.NewProvingKey(curve); nativePK.WriteTo(buf); iciPK.ReadFrom(buf)
```

## 3. Benchmark patterns + CPU-vs-GPU plonk bench recipe

Existing benchmarks (grep `func Benchmark` over backend/ and internal/):
- backend/groth16/groth16_test.go:58/70/90 — `BenchmarkSetup`/`BenchmarkProver`/`BenchmarkVerifier`; per-curve `b.Run(curve.String(), ...)`; `refCircuit` of 40000 `api.Mul(X,X)` constraints (lines 120-156); prover bench uses `groth16.DummySetup` to skip full setup; `b.ResetTimer()` then `for i := 0; i < b.N; i++`.
- backend/plonk/plonk_test.go:194/206/226 — same shape with `referenceCircuit(curve)` = `(1<<12)-3` constraints (line 320), real `plonk.Setup`, `unsafekzg.NewSRS(ccs, WithFSCache())`.
- backend/plonk/plonk_test.go:259 **`BenchmarkLargeProver`** — the direct model for GPU benching: `const nbConstraints = 1<<21 + 100_000` → domain `1<<22`; bn254 only; compile scs; `unsafekzg.NewSRS(ccs, unsafekzg.WithFSCache())`; Setup; one sanity prove+verify before timing; then b.N loop of `plonk.Prove`. Witness trick: `good.X = 1; good.Y = 1` (1*1=1 fixed point) avoids the big-exponent computation used by referenceCircuit (which sets Y = 2^(2^n) mod r — that big.Int Exp is itself slow at 2^21, so the X=1 trick matters at large sizes).
- Others (mpcsetup, gkr, tinyfield) are not relevant patterns.
- internal/backend/circuits (circuits.go:11-17 `TestCircuit` registry, ~30 tiny circuits) is used by root `integration_test.go` TestIntegrationAPI and constraint tests — correctness only, not benchmarking; the circuits are all O(1) size and useless for perf.

**Recipe for plonk prove CPU vs GPU at 2^16..2^22** (new file, `//go:build icicle`, suggested location `backend/accelerated/icicle/plonk/bench_test.go`):
- Circuit to scale: the existing `refCircuit` multiplication chain (plonk_test.go:305-317) — `for i := 0; i < nbConstraints; i++ { X = api.Mul(X, X) }; api.AssertIsEqual(X, Y)`. Each `api.Mul` emits 1 SparseR1C; AssertIsEqual adds 1; 1 public variable adds 1 placeholder row in setup. To land exactly on domain 2^k set `nbConstraints = (1<<k) - 8` (any small slack works since the domain rounds up: domain = NextPowerOfTwo(nbConstraints + nbPublic); copy the `-3` slack from referenceCircuit or the `+100_000` overshoot style from BenchmarkLargeProver and just log `ccs.GetNbConstraints()`).
- Structure:
```go
for k := 16; k <= 22; k++ {
    circuit := refCircuit{nbConstraints: (1<<k) - 8}
    ccs, _ := frontend.Compile(curve.ScalarField(), scs.NewBuilder, &circuit)
    srs, srsLagrange, _ := unsafekzg.NewSRS(ccs, unsafekzg.WithFSCache()) // FS cache mandatory: bw6-761 2^22 SRS generation is many minutes
    pk, vk, _ := plonk.Setup(ccs, srs, srsLagrange)
    iciPK := icicle_plonk.NewProvingKey(curve); /* WriteTo/ReadFrom round trip */
    // sanity: GPU prove once + CPU verify (fail fast on corruption)
    b.Run(fmt.Sprintf("%s/2^%d/cpu", curve, k), func(b *testing.B){ for range b.N { plonk.Prove(ccs, pk, w) } })
    b.Run(fmt.Sprintf("%s/2^%d/gpu", curve, k), func(b *testing.B){ for range b.N { icicle_plonk.Prove(ccs, iciPK, w) } })
}
```
- Witness: X=1, Y=1 (BenchmarkLargeProver pattern, lines 269-272).
- Invocation: `go test -tags=icicle -run='^$' -bench=BenchmarkPlonkProve -benchtime=3x -timeout=0 -count=1 ./backend/accelerated/icicle/plonk/` (use `-benchtime=Nx` not time-based, so the expensive Setup amortizes predictably; `-timeout=0` because 2^22 setups take minutes; default 10m test timeout WILL fire otherwise).
- SRS size is determined automatically by `unsafekzg.NewSRS` from the compiled ccs (NextPowerOfTwo(nbConstraints+nbPublic)+3) — never hand-compute it. FS cache files at ~/.gnark/kzg are per (curve,size): for the full 4-curve × 7-size matrix expect tens of GB (bw6-761 G1 points are 192 bytes raw ×2 SRSes ×(2^22+3)); consider `WithCacheDir` on a big disk, and consider benchmarking bw6-761 only at smaller sizes (8 GB VRAM also caps bw6 first — its points are 3× bn254 size). GPU warmup is amortized by the sanity prove before `b.ResetTimer()` (warmUpDevice sync.Once runs on first Prove).
- If GPU pinning is implemented (cf. `icicle.WithPinKeysToGPU`, opts.go:119-124, and groth16's PinnedG1Device in bn254/provingkey.go:21-27), bench both pinned and unpinned variants — that's the PCIe-transfer axis the plan's risk section cares about.

## 4. Race detector / -tags interplay

## PART A — Ground-truth ICICLE NTT semantics (verified at kernel level, icicle-gnark v3.2.2)

All paths below are under /home/work/go/pkg/mod/github.com/ingonyama-zk/icicle-gnark/v3@v3.2.2 (abbrev. ICICLE/) and /home/work/go/pkg/mod/github.com/consensys/gnark-crypto@v0.20.1 (abbrev. GC/). gnark repo = /home/work/repositories/gnark.

**A1. Coset convention — ICICLE matches gnark's OnCoset exactly, same CosetGen both directions.**
- Forward+coset = shift-then-NTT: input is element-wise pre-multiplied by powers CosetGen^j BEFORE the butterflies. Radix-2: `direct_coset = (!inverse && is_on_coset)` then `BatchMulKernel` on d_input — ICICLE/icicle/backend/cuda/src/ntt/ntt.cuh:342-346. Mixed-radix: `if (is_on_coset && !is_inverse)` pre-multiply — ICICLE/icicle/backend/cuda/src/ntt/mixed_radix_ntt.cu:976-983. This is gnark `Domain.FFT(a, ..., fft.OnCoset())` which pre-multiplies by cosetTable — GC/ecc/bn254/fr/fft/fft.go:44-82.
- Inverse+coset = NTT-then-unshift: AFTER butterflies (and after any output reordering), output is multiplied by CosetGen^{-j} and by 1/n. Radix-2: ntt.cuh:375-381 (`-coset_gen_index` + `NormalizeKernel` with `S::inv_log_size(logn)`). Mixed-radix: mixed_radix_ntt.cu:1009-1014 (`linear_twiddle + n_twiddles`, `-coset_gen_index`); normalization `is_normalize = is_inverse` at mixed_radix_ntt.cu:941. For a CosetGen NOT in the twiddle subgroup, the inverse direction explicitly builds powers of `S::inverse(config.coset_gen)` — ntt.cuh:689-703 (esp. line 697). This is gnark `FFTInverse(a, ..., fft.OnCoset())` post-multiply by cosetTableInv·CardinalityInv — GC fft.go:144-192. **You pass the SAME CosetGen value for forward and inverse; ICICLE inverts internally.** ICICLE inverse ALWAYS applies 1/n (matching gnark CardinalityInv at fft.go:145-151), coset or not.
- The coset power table is always reordered internally to match the data order at the multiply point: `reverse_coset` per ordering — mixed_radix_ntt.cu:944-974 (kRN fwd: NaturalToRev; kNR inv: NaturalToRev; kNN: None; kMN fwd / kNM inv: NaturalToMixedRev). Radix-2 equivalently passes `dit` (fwd) / `!dit` (inv) as the `bitrev` flag to BatchMulKernel — ntt.cuh:345-346, 377-378 — whose indexing is `scalar_id = bitrev ? __brev(tid)>>(32-logn) : tid; out[tid] = scalar_vec[(scalar_id*step) % n_scalars] * in[tid]` — ICICLE/icicle/backend/cuda/include/utils_kernels.h:14-31. So ICICLE's bit-reversed coset application is EXACTLY gnark's `scalingVectorRev` semantics (gnark fft.go:54-61).

**A2. Ordering enum** (ICICLE/wrappers/golang/core/ntt.go:18-27; ICICLE/icicle/include/icicle/ntt.h:37-44): KNN, KNR, KRN, KRR, KNM, KMN. Radix-2 mapping: kNN = explicit input bit-reverse + DIT; kNR≡kNM = DIF; kRN≡kMN = DIT; — ntt.cuh:616-637. Mixed-radix: M = "digit-reversed mixed order", NOT bit-reversed — ntt.h:32-35, mixed_radix_ntt.cu:947-974.

**A3. Algorithm selection is a heuristic on {logn, batch_size, columns_batch, ext}** — ntt.cuh:569-595: logn≥16 → mixed-radix; logn≤11 → radix-2; else `logn+log2(batch) <= 18` → radix-2. **Consequence (the question's "scale between KNM/KMN" issue, now resolved definitively): the M-order intermediate is algorithm-dependent (plain bit-reverse under radix-2, digit-reverse under mixed-radix), so a user-supplied scaling vector between a KNM/KMN pair has no stable device layout. It is only safe if (a) nothing index-dependent touches the intermediate, or (b) you pin the algorithm via ConfigExtension key `CUDA_NTT_ALGORITHM` (core/ntt.go:37-38) AND both calls of the pair use identical {logn, batch} so the heuristic resolves identically.** The groth16 precedent only does order-agnostic VecOps (Mul/Sub with all operands in the same M order) between the pair — gnark backend/accelerated/icicle/groth16/bn254/icicle.go:1419-1428 (KNM iNTT, then KMN forward coset NTT), 1450-1462 (VecOps in M order). For Plonk, the per-round scale by shifter^j does NOT need a scaling vector at all — it IS a coset shift and must be expressed via CosetGen (see Part C).

**A4. CosetGen fast vs slow path.** `domain.coset_index` only contains 1, PR, PR^2, PR^4, PR^8, ... (powers-of-two powers of the InitDomain primitive root) — ntt.cuh:500-509. Any other CosetGen takes the "arbitrary coset" path: a host-side O(size) power-table build + cudaMemcpyAsync PER NTT CALL — ntt.cuh:689-703. gnark's multiplicative generators are u = 5 (bn254), 22 (bls12-377), 7 (bls12-381), 15 (bw6-761) — GC/ecc/{curve}/fr/fft/domain.go:58-61 — never in the subgroup, so **every CosetGen involving u is the slow path**. CosetGen = w_{4n} (domain1.Generator) IS the fast path whenever InitDomain max size M ≥ 4n (w_{4n} = PR^{M/4n}, a power-of-two power). This is why groth16-ICICLE deliberately uses w_{2n} (fft.Generator(2*Cardinality)) as its coset instead of CPU groth16's FrMultiplicativeGen — gnark backend/accelerated/icicle/groth16/bn254/icicle.go:96 (gen), 128-130 (CosetGenerator from gen.Bits()), 131-132+163 (same gen used as InitDomain root). Plonk cannot freely swap u out without re-deriving the host-side constants that depend on it (orderingConstraint id at prove.go:909, precomputedDenominators at prove.go:1002-1007, evaluateXnMinusOneDomainBigCoset at prove.go:1327-1350) — a design decision, not a correctness blocker (the coset is prover-internal; the verifier never sees it).

**A5. CosetGen representation:** `[fr.Limbs*2]uint32` little-endian limbs of the STANDARD (non-Montgomery) value, via `gen.Bits()` + `ConvertUint64ArrToUint32Arr` — gnark backend/accelerated/icicle/groth16/bn254/icicle.go:128-130, backend/accelerated/icicle/groth16/bn254/provingkey.go:19. Data vectors may stay in Montgomery form through NTTs (linearity; groth16 runs NTTs before FromMontgomery — icicle.go:1421-1428 vs 1452), but CosetGen itself must be standard-form limbs.

**A6. Wrapper API:** `Ntt(scalars, dir, &cfg, results)` with `size = input.Len()/cfg.BatchSize` — ICICLE/wrappers/golang/core/ntt.go:75-100; per-curve `GetDefaultNttConfig()` returns CosetGen = one — ICICLE/wrappers/golang/curves/bn254/ntt/ntt.go:30-39. Batch: `BatchSize int32`, `ColumnsBatch bool` (false = polynomials concatenated contiguously) — core/ntt.go:40-59. **The Go wrapper exposes NO device bit-reverse permutation** (VecOps = Sub/Add/Mul only — core/vec_ops.go:11-17), so any shape that on CPU ends with an explicit `ToRegular()` bit-reverse MUST instead be expressed by choosing an ordering that lands natural (KNN/KRN/KMN).

**A7. InitDomain sizing:** NTT size must be ≤ domain max (ntt.cuh:651-658); twiddle striding handles smaller sizes. Plonk needs M ≥ domain1.Cardinality = 4·sizeSystem (8· when sizeSystem<6 — gnark backend/plonk/bn254/prove.go:247-251), vs groth16's 2n; the per-device domain cache `nttDomainMaxByDevice` (icicle.go:134-168) must be requested at 4n/8n.

## PART B — CPU-side authoritative spec of the five shapes (exact lines)

All polynomials entering computeNumerator are Lagrange/Regular: L,R,O (prove.go:331-339), Z (prove.go:645-656, Form at 654), ZS = ShallowClone().Shift(1) of Z (prove.go:602; view-only, skipped by batchApply — prove.go batchApply explicitly `continue`s on id_ZS; shift realized at read time via GetCoeff — GC iop/polynomial.go:152-158), Qk clone (prove.go:351-373), Ql/Qr/Qm/Qo/Qk/Qcp/S1/S2/S3 (setup.go:204-228), cCommitments (prove.go:299). Round-loop: prove.go:996-1087. shifters[0]=domain1.FrMultiplicativeGen=u, shifters[i≥1]=domain1.Generator=w_{4n} (prove.go:936-941). Effective coset round i = u·w_{4n}^i (prove.go:998). domain0 and domain1 share FrMultiplicativeGen=u (prove.go:236,248-250; GC domain.go:178).

1. **Shape (1)** prove.go:1038 `p.ToCanonical(s.domain0, nbTasks)` from lagrangeRegular → GC iop/polynomial.go:333-335: `FFTInverse(DIF)`, Layout→BitReverse. Math: out = BitRev(INTT(in))·(1/n) (GC fft.go:136-137,145-151). No coset.
2. **Shape (2)** prove.go:1041-1053: pointwise multiply the bit-reversed canonical coefficients by `scalingVectorRev` = BitRev(powers of shifters[i]) (built at prove.go:983-986 for round 0 = cosetTable of u; prove.go:1018-1028 for rounds ≥1 = powers of w_{4n}); then prove.go:1056 `p.ToLagrange(s.domain0).ToRegular()` from canonicalBitReverse → GC polynomial.go:301-303: `FFT(DIT)` (NO OnCoset — the coset shift is the manual scale), Layout→Regular; ToRegular is a no-op. The scaling is CUMULATIVE: coefficients stay scaled by (u·w^{i})^j across rounds (only blinding polys get unscaled per-round — prove.go:1009-1017, 1078-1086, host-side, degree ≤3).
3. **Shape (3) restore pass** prove.go:1090-1114: from lagrangeRegular, `p.ToCanonical(s.domain0, 8)` = FFTInverse(DIF) → Canonical/BitReverse (GC polynomial.go:333-335), `.ToRegular()` = EXPLICIT utils.BitReverse (GC polynomial.go:266-273), then `scalePowers(p, cs)` with cs = (u·w_{4n}^{rho-1})^{-1} (= inverse of Π shifters, prove.go:1094-1099; scalePowers def prove.go:1172-1180) → pristine Canonical/Regular coefficients, consumed later on host (linearized poly prove.go:1418,1433-1437; gated by chRestoreLRO at prove.go:627).
4. **Shape (4)** prove.go:1420 `s.trace.Qk.ToCanonical(s.domain0).ToRegular()` from lagrangeRegular: FFTInverse(DIF) + explicit BitReverse → Canonical/Regular, 1/n included, no coset, size n.
5. **Shape (5)** divideByZH, prove.go:1287-1323. Input contract: LagrangeCoset/BitReverse on domain1 (enforced at 1300; produced at 1119 from cres assembled bit-reversed at 1070-1076: `cres[bitrev_{4n}(rho*j+i)] = buf[j]`, i.e. natural index k=rho·j+i ↔ evaluation at u·w_{4n}^k). Steps: (a) pointwise multiply by 1/(Z_H) — rho-periodic table indexed `[bitrev(i) % rho]` because data is bit-reversed (1312-1317, table from 1327-1350); (b) prove.go:1320 `a.ToCanonical(bigDomain).ToRegular()` from lagrangeCosetBitReverse → GC polynomial.go:342-344: `FFTInverse(DIT, OnCoset())`, Layout→Regular (DIT: bit-rev in, natural out; coset post-multiply u^{-j}·(1/n) in NATURAL order — GC fft.go:154-175; domain1 is WithoutPrecompute so the on-the-fly branch fft.go:162-173 runs, same math). ToRegular is a no-op (comment 1319). **Result MUST be Canonical/Regular natural** because h1/h2/h3 take CONTIGUOUS coefficient slices `[0 : n+2]`, `[n+2 : 2(n+2)]`, `[2(n+2) : 3(n+2)]` — prove.go:689-724 — fed to kzg.Commit against the natural-order canonical SRS (prove.go:1263-1282).

## PART C — The exact ICICLE invocations

Per-curve `cfg := icicle_ntt.GetDefaultNttConfig()`; CosetGen as standard limbs (A5); BatchSize/ColumnsBatch as noted; one `InitDomain` with the primitive root of order ≥ domain1.Cardinality (4n, or 8n when sizeSystem<6).

**Shape (1) — numerator-round iNTT.**
- CPU-layout-faithful: `Ntt(buf, KInverse, cfg{Ordering: KNR, CosetGen: one, BatchSize: k, ColumnsBatch: false})`, size n per poly, k polys concatenated. Output = Canonical/BitReverse, 1/n included. Bit-identical to FFTInverse(DIF)+CardinalityInv.
- Recommended (paired with shape 2 below, groth16 pattern): `Ordering: KNM` (icicle.go:1419,1425 precedent) — ONLY if the very next call is the shape-(2) forward with KMN, same buffer, same {logn, batch}, nothing index-dependent in between (A3). Nothing else may read the M-order intermediate.
- Device-native alternative: `Ordering: KNN` (output Canonical natural; costs one extra reorder vs KNM/KMN but the intermediate is well-defined).

**Shape (2) — scaled forward NTT with effective coset.** The CPU "scalingVectorRev multiply + FFT(DIT)" is EXACTLY an ICICLE forward coset NTT; do NOT implement the scale as a separate VecOp.
- Two mutually exclusive CosetGen accountings:
  - (a) Mirror-CPU (stateful, coefficients stay scaled across rounds, exactly prove.go:1041-1056): per round i, `Ntt(buf, KForward, cfg{Ordering: KMN (paired with KNM iNTT) or KRN (paired with KNR iNTT) or KNN (paired with KNN), CosetGen: shifters[i]})` where shifters[0] = u = domain1.FrMultiplicativeGen, shifters[i≥1] = w_{4n} = domain1.Generator. Round 0 hits the arbitrary-coset slow path (u not in subgroup, A4); rounds 1..rho-1 hit the fast subgroup-index path (w_{4n} = PR^{M/4n}). With KRN the coset powers are applied bit-reverse-indexed to the bit-reversed input (mixed_radix_ntt.cu:955; ntt.cuh:345 with dit=true) — literally scalingVectorRev. Output = Lagrange/Regular (natural) evaluations on coset u·w^i·H, as required by the constraint evaluator, which is index-dependent (twiddles0[index] at prove.go:909, precomputedDenominators[index] at 929/1002-1007, ZS rotation-by-1 at 972 / GetCoeff) — so the Lagrange-side buffer MUST be natural order; M order is unusable there.
  - (b) Stateless (keep pristine canonical c_j on device once; skip shape (1) per round entirely): per round i a single `Ntt(coeffs, KForward, cfg{Ordering: KNN or KNR-as-needed, CosetGen: u·w_{4n}^i})`. Mathematically identical; every round takes the arbitrary-coset slow path (u·w^i never a 2^k-th power of PR). Halves the NTT count per round but adds rho host-side O(4 separate n) coset builds; benchmark before choosing.
  - Do NOT mix (a) and (b): in (a) the input already carries coset_{i-1} scaling and you pass the per-round shifter; in (b) the input is pristine and you pass the cumulative coset.
- Batch: all k≈12+ same-size-n polynomials (id_L..id_Qci..., minus ZS and the skip list) in one contiguous DeviceSlice, BatchSize=k, ColumnsBatch=false; the per-call arbitrary-coset table (length n) is shared across the batch (ntt.cuh:689-703 builds per call, not per batch element). Keep the SAME BatchSize for both halves of a KNM/KMN pair (A3 corruption hazard).

**Shape (3) — restore pass.** Single fused call replaces iNTT + explicit BitReverse + scalePowers: `Ntt(buf, KInverse, cfg{Ordering: KNN (input natural Lagrange from last round) , CosetGen: u·w_{4n}^{rho-1}, BatchSize: k})`. ICICLE inverse-coset = plain iNTT then post-multiply by (u·w^{rho-1})^{-j}·(1/n) in natural order (A1; kNN inverse has reverse_coset=None — mixed_radix_ntt.cu:947-950 falls through with None) — which is precisely ToCanonical(1/n) + ToRegular + scalePowers(cs), cs=(u·w^{rho-1})^{-1} (prove.go:1094-1106). Output Canonical/Regular pristine coefficients; copy back to host (linearization/KZG consume them there). KNM is FORBIDDEN here (no later NTT absorbs M order; no device bit/digit-reverse exists in the wrapper — A6). Arbitrary-coset slow path (contains u). The s.bp blinding-poly scalePowers (prove.go:1109-1111) stays on CPU.

**Shape (4) — trace.Qk.** `Ntt(qk, KInverse, cfg{Ordering: KNN, CosetGen: one, BatchSize: 1})`, size n. KNN fuses CPU's FFTInverse(DIF)+explicit BitReverse into one call; 1/n automatic. (KNR would reproduce the intermediate Canonical/BitReverse and then dead-end — no device bit-reverse.) Note this runs in computeLinearizedPolynomial on the un-completed trace.Qk (prove.go:1420), not the completed clone s.x[id_Qk]; it can equally stay on CPU — it is one size-n iNTT.

**Shape (5) — divideByZH, THE silent-corruption axis.** Required output: Canonical/Regular NATURAL (Part B5). Two correct forms:
- Mirror-CPU: assemble cres bit-reversed exactly as prove.go:1073; VecOp-Mul by a precomputed length-4n device vector ZHinvRev[r] = xnMinusOneInverseLagrangeCoset[bitrev_{4n}(r) % rho] (analogous to groth16's DenDevice pattern, icicle.go:108-121, but rho-periodic instead of constant); then `Ntt(cres, KInverse, cfg{Ordering: KRN, CosetGen: u = domain1.FrMultiplicativeGen, BatchSize: 1})`, size = domain1.Cardinality. ICICLE kRN inverse: bit-rev in → DIT butterflies → natural out → coset unshift u^{-j}·(1/n) applied NATURAL-indexed (reverse_coset=None for kRN inverse — mixed_radix_ntt.cu:955; radix-2 `!dit`=false — ntt.cuh:378) — bit-identical to gnark FFTInverse(DIT, OnCoset) at GC fft.go:154-175 / polynomial.go:342-344.
- Device-native: assemble cres natural (`cres_nat[rho*j+i] = buf_i[j]`, a stride-rho scatter), VecOp-Mul by ZHinv_nat[k] = table[k % rho], then `Ntt(cres, KInverse, cfg{Ordering: KNN, CosetGen: u})` → identical output.
- **NEVER Ordering=KNR here.** The question's diagnosis is confirmed by code: groth16-ICICLE's final inverse coset NTT uses KNR (icicle.go:1470-1476) ONLY because CPU groth16 leaves h bit-reversed (`domain.FFTInverse(a, fft.DIF, fft.OnCoset())`, backend/groth16/bn254/prove.go:386, no bit-reverse after) and pk.G1.Z was bit-reversed at setup to match (backend/groth16/bn254/setup.go:247). Plonk's SRS is natural-order and h1/h2/h3 are contiguous slices (prove.go:689-724) — KNR output would be a valid-looking buffer whose commitment is wrong: silent proof corruption. Also KNM is equally forbidden (digit-reversed, algorithm-dependent).

## PART D — Pre-flight unit test matrix (write before any prover code)

For each curve {bn254, bls12-377, bls12-381, bw6-761}, sizes n ∈ {2^10 (radix-2 regime), 2^14 (heuristic boundary), 2^17 (mixed-radix regime)} per ntt.cuh:592-595, random vector v, against gnark Domain (and Domain1 with WithoutPrecompute to match prove.go:248-250):
1. Ntt(KInverse, KNR, gen=1) == FFTInverse(v, DIF) [+1/n]   → shape 1.
2. Ntt(KForward, KRN, CosetGen=g) on BitRev(c) == {c·rev-scaled by g^j; FFT DIT} i.e. == FFT(c_scaled, DIT) where c was pre-multiplied via scalingVectorRev — for g ∈ {u, w_{4n}} (one arbitrary-path, one fast-path gen) → shape 2(a).
3. Ntt(KForward, KNN, CosetGen=u·w^i) == ToLagrangeCoset-style FFT(DIT/DIF, OnCoset) reference for cumulative coset → shape 2(b).
4. Ntt(KInverse, KNN, CosetGen=u·w^{rho-1}) == ToCanonical(lagrangeRegular)+ToRegular+scalePowers(cs) → shape 3.
5. Ntt(KInverse, KRN, CosetGen=u) on BitRev(evals) == FFTInverse(evals_bitrev, DIT, OnCoset) == divideByZH's transform → shape 5 (assert NATURAL output: compare coefficient-slice commitments, not just vectors).
6. KNM-then-KMN round-trip with CosetGen on the second call, at a size near the radix2/mixed boundary AND with differing BatchSize between the two calls, to demonstrate/document the algorithm-mismatch corruption mode and the CUDA_NTT_ALGORITHM pin (core/ntt.go:37-38).
7. Representation: all of the above with inputs in Montgomery form (CosetGen always standard limbs via .Bits()) to validate the linearity argument used by groth16 (icicle.go:1421-1428 NTT-before-FromMontgomery).

Key files for the design phase: gnark/backend/plonk/bn254/prove.go:996-1119, 1287-1350, 689-724, 1420; GC/ecc/bn254/fr/iop/polynomial.go:288-391; GC/ecc/bn254/fr/fft/fft.go:31-194; gnark/backend/accelerated/icicle/groth16/bn254/icicle.go:96-168, 1395-1488; ICICLE wrappers/golang/core/ntt.go, curves/*/ntt/ntt.go; ICICLE icicle/backend/cuda/src/ntt/ntt.cuh:300-381, 500-509, 569-595, 598-703; mixed_radix_ntt.cu:910-1015; include/utils_kernels.h:14-31.

gap_answers.question: Is offloading computeNumerator feasible at all with icicle-gnark v3.2.2's primitive set, and if not, what is the quantitative case for MSM-only scope? How are the per-index terms of allConstraints handled on device — blinding-poly evals, the ZS rotate-by-1, computeLagrangeOneOnCoset's serial batch inversion, alpha/beta/gamma broadcasts, degree-4 Montgomery products, and the bitrev scatter?
gap_answers.answer:
VERDICT. A direct translation of computeNumerator (backend/plonk/bn254/prove.go:841-1123) to icicle-gnark v3.2.2 is NOT expressible with the wrapper's primitive set: every per-index term needs a workaround, and three of the six problem terms (scalar broadcast, inversion, permutation) have no device primitive at all. It IS feasible as a restructured pipeline where all index-dependent/scalar terms are precomputed host-side as n-vectors and uploaded, with explicit Montgomery-power bookkeeping — but the measured profile shows the constraint closure proper is only ~7% of prover CPU at every size from 2^16 to 2^22, so even a perfect offload of it buys <=1.08x. The dominant offload targets, in measured order, are MSM (38-55% of samples) and the FFT machinery (30-48%, of which the computeNumerator per-coset FFT pipeline is 13-19%). Quantitative case for MSM-first scope is at the end.

== 1. Complete icicle-gnark v3.2.2 primitive inventory (bn254; identical structure for bls12377/bls12381/bw6761 — wrappers/golang/curves/ lists exactly those 4 dirs) ==
- vecOps: ONE function, VecOp(a,b,out,cfg,op) with op in {Sub, Add, Mul} only (wrappers/golang/curves/bn254/vecOps/vec_ops.go:12-31; enum at wrappers/golang/core/vec_ops.go:13-17; C surface is exactly bn254_vector_{mul,add,sub} in vecOps/include/vec_ops.h). VecOpCheck panics unless len(a)==len(b)==len(out) (core/vec_ops.go:63-78) — so NO scalar broadcast of any kind; constants must be full-length vectors.
- ntt: Ntt(scalars, dir, cfg, results) with NTTConfig.CosetGen and Ordering in {KNN,KNR,KRN,KRR,KNM,KMN} (curves/bn254/ntt/ntt.go:15-27; core/ntt.go:18-26,49-50) — bit-reversal is absorbable only as part of an NTT, never standalone. InitDomain/ReleaseDomain (ntt.go:47-59). WARNING: ntt.GetRootOfUnity (ntt.go:40-45) is broken — it casts a C pointer to a Go slice header (`*(*[]uint32)(unsafe.Pointer(cRes))`) and segfaults (reproduced on the dev box); the Groth16 integration avoids it by computing the generator host-side via gnark-crypto fft.Generator + ConvertUint64ArrToUint32Arr (backend/accelerated/icicle/groth16/bn254/icicle.go:96-99,128-133,163). Plonk must do the same.
- msm: Msm + PrecomputeBases (curves/bn254/msm/msm.go:14-32), MSMConfig has AreBasesMontgomeryForm/AreScalarsMontgomeryForm (used at groth16 icicle.go:862-863,909-910,1232).
- Montgomery conversion: ToMontgomery/FromMontgomery on whole scalar slices (curves/bn254/scalar_field.go:171-184), affine/projective variants (curve.go:171-200).
- runtime/core: Malloc/Free, MemSet (byte-fill only — can build zero vectors, cannot build arbitrary field-constant vectors; runtime/memory.go:50-59), CopyToDevice/CopyFromDevice (+async) ONLY — there is NO device-to-device copy (runtime/memory.go:62-87; runtime/include/runtime.h:27-30 has only icicle_copy_to_host/icicle_copy_to_device). DeviceSlice.Range/RangeTo/RangeFrom views (core/slice.go:59-118) — contiguous only, no stride, no wraparound. No pinned host memory API (only the capability flag DeviceProperties.SupportsPinnedMemory, runtime/device.go:21) — all PCIe copies are pageable.
- ABSENT entirely (grepped all of wrappers/golang): gather/scatter/permutation/transpose kernels, vector inversion, reductions/sums, polynomial-evaluation kernels, scalar-by-vector ops.
- Operational landmine (measured): device binding is per-OS-thread. Calls made outside icicle_runtime.RunOnDevice (runtime/runtime.go:93-96, which does runtime.LockOSThread) silently dispatch to the CPU backend after goroutine migration — observed vecMul at 2^22 of 25.7ms (CPU backend) vs 0.70ms (CUDA) = 37x, and an NTT abort "Size is too large for domain... domain_max_size = 0" from cpu_ntt. Every GPU call in the Plonk integration must live inside RunOnDevice (Groth16 does this everywhere, e.g. icicle.go:118,1438-1440).

== 2. Term-by-term: how each per-index term of allConstraints maps (or fails to map) to the device ==
Context: computeNumerator runs rho = domain1/domain0 = 4 coset iterations (prove.go:936, 996; domain1 = 4*sizeSystem at prove.go:250). Per iteration it (a) re-FFTs all polynomials in s.x onto the next coset — batchApply closure at 1035-1057: ToCanonical (INTT_n), elementwise scale by scalingVector (1048-1053), ToLagrange (NTT_n), ToRegular; s.x holds 13+2c entries (id_L..id_Qci, prove.go:44-59, allocated at 231) of which ZS shares Z's storage (ShallowClone().Shift(1) at 602; batchApply skips id_ZS at 1154-1159) => 12+2c distinct size-n vectors; (b) evaluates allConstraints elementwise via iop.Evaluate (1061-1068; gnark-crypto iop/expressions.go:27-75 — embarrassingly parallel, layout handled by GetCoeff); (c) scatters buf into cres in bit-reversed interleaved order (1069-1076).

(1) Blinding-poly evals at twiddles0[index] (prove.go:962-973). s.bp orders are 1,1,1,2 (prove.go:71-76), i.e. 2-3 coefficients, rescaled in place each iteration (1009-1017 forward, 1080-1086 inverse). Device mapping: y_i = b0 + b1*t_i (+ b2*t_i^2) needs scalar broadcasts (none exist). Workarounds: (i) materialize b0,b1,b2 as constant n-vectors Den-style (the Groth16 precedent: a single scalar denI is replicated into an n-element host array and uploaded, icicle.go:100-125) + 2 vecMul + 2 vecAdd against a device-resident twiddles0 vector — ~5 constant-vector uploads per iteration; or (ii) precompute the 5 blinding-eval n-vectors host-side (~10n mul/add, ~10ms at 2^20) and upload 5n*32B = 160MB/iteration at 2^20 (~25ms at measured 6.5GB/s). The ZS blinding eval needs the rotated twiddle twiddles0[(index+1)%n] (972) — trivial host-side, not expressible as a device view. Note twiddles0 itself is built host-side as a full n-vector anyway (843-858).

(2) ZS rotate-by-1. s.x[id_ZS] = Z shifted by 1 (prove.go:602); reads resolve to coefficients[(i+rho*shift)%n] (gnark-crypto iop/polynomial.go:152-164 — Regular layout case at :157). The %n wraparound makes it non-contiguous: DeviceSlice.Range cannot express it, and there is no D2D copy to materialize a rotated buffer. Workarounds: (i) emulate rotation with 2 vecop Adds against a MemSet(0) zero vector over Range views: out[0:n-1] = Add(Z[1:n], zero), out[n-1:n] = Add(Z[0:1], zero) — legal (lengths match per call) but a hack; (ii) split every vecop that touches ZS into two Range-pair calls ([0,n-1) and the last element) — doubles launches for ~6 ops; (iii) in a big-domain restructuring (below), ZS on domain1 = rotate-by-rho of Z's 4n values — same trick, still 2 pseudo-copies. Critically, rotation only works in NATURAL layout; in bitrev layout a rotate-by-1 is a full scatter (impossible — see (6)). This forces a layout decision for the whole pipeline.

(3) computeLagrangeOneOnCoset + serial batch inversion. lone_i = (coset^n - 1)/n * 1/(coset*w^i - 1) (prove.go:379-385) using precomputedDenominators built and inverted per iteration (993-994, 1002-1007) with batchInvert (1130-1141) — an inherently serial prefix-product chain. No inversion vecop exists. BUT measured cost is ~0.2% of prover samples at all sizes (focus 'plonk/bn254.batchInvert': 0.17% at 2^16, 0.23% at 2^20, 0.20% at 2^22) — keep on host, upload the finished lone n-vector (or fold into other precomputed vectors): 32MB/iteration at 2^20, ~5ms. Not a blocker; it does pin one host-sync point per coset iteration.

(4) alpha/beta/gamma scalar broadcasts. Used at 909 (id = twiddle*coset*beta), 911-913 + 916-918 (gamma adds), 912-913 (cs, css = coset shifts squared, 888-890), 956-958 (beta*S1/S2/S3), 978 (two alpha-folds). No broadcast vecop => each scalar needs a full n-element constant vector (Den-style fill + 32n upload + optional FromMontgomery, groth16 icicle.go:108-125). gamma/beta are known after round 1 (deriveGammaAndBeta, prove.go:509-519), but alpha is derived only mid-proof, after the Z commitment: deriveAlpha at 542-550, called from computeQuotient at 593-596 gated on <-s.chZ (586-591), immediately before computeNumerator (604). So the alpha constant vector (128MB at 2^22) can only be built and uploaded on the critical path (~20ms upload + host fill). Cheaper alternatives: fold beta into S1/S2/S3 and beta*coset into the precomputed id-vector host-side; for alpha, note 978 is Horner — needs alpha as a multiplicand of full vectors twice, so either 1 constant vector + 2 vecMul, or fold alpha into the host-uploaded lone vector (alpha^2 * lone) and alpha into... the b-term cannot be folded (b is device-computed), so at least one alpha constant vector is unavoidable in a full-device closure.

(5) Degree-4 Montgomery products. gnark fr.Elements are Montgomery residues (xR); ICICLE vecMul multiplies raw residues, so a product of k Montgomery operands carries R^k — R^(k-1) excess. Groth16's rule — exactly one standard-form operand per Mul — is visible in computeH: FromMontgomery(a) before Mul(a,b) keeps abR^1 (icicle.go:1452-1457), Sub form-agnostic (1458), then Mul with the pre-converted standard-form DenDevice (FromMontgomery at setup, icicle.go:121) keeps R^1 (1461), final FromMontgomery after the INTT (1480). This does not generalize to computeNumerator because (a) gateConstraint (869-886) SUMS terms of mixed product degree: Ql*L (R^2), Qm*L*R (R^3), Qk (R^1) — cross-degree additions are silently wrong without normalization; converting the 9+2c proving-key-side vectors (Ql,Qr,Qm,Qo,Qk,S1,S2,S3,Qci) to standard form per iteration fixes the degree-2 terms (9 FromMontgomery passes, ~177us each at 2^20) but Qm*L*R still needs one more conversion on a temporary; and (b) orderingConstraint's r = a*b*c*Z and l = a*b*c*ZS (914, 919) have FOUR unavoidably-Montgomery operands — a,b,c are gamma/beta-sums of witness values computed on device (911-913, 916-918), so no operand can be pre-converted; each chain needs either 3 FromMontgomery passes on temporaries or one vecMul by a precomputed R^-3 constant vector (itself a Den-style broadcast). Net: ~6-12 extra full-vector passes per iteration plus pervasive form bookkeeping with zero type-safety — feasible, high silent-corruption risk.

(6) Bitrev scatter cres[bits.Reverse64(rho*j+i)>>mm] = buf[j] (1069-1076). No permutation/gather kernel exists. Structure helps: rev_m(rho*j+i) = rev_lg(rho)(i)*n + rev_lg(n)(j), so iteration i fills the CONTIGUOUS block [rev(i)*n, (rev(i)+1)*n) of cres with bitrev(buf) — expressible as a Range write IF buf is produced in bitrev layout. But bitrev layout conflicts with the ZS rotation (see (2)), which demands natural layout; and a natural-layout buf cannot be bit-reversed on device (no kernel). Resolution options: (i) materialize ZS naturally, bitrev everything else: run the closure in bitrev layout (elementwise ops are layout-agnostic; all host-precomputed index vectors — twiddles-derived id, lone, blinding evals — uploaded pre-bitreversed for free), and materialize ZS by rotating Z BEFORE the layout-sensitive step, i.e. produce a rotated copy in natural layout then NTT both... (forces an extra NTT pair for ZS); (ii) restructure to ONE 4n coset NTT per polynomial (ICICLE Ntt supports arbitrary CosetGen + KNR/KRN/KNM/KMN; exact Groth16 precedent at icicle.go:1416-1428 (KNM INTT then coset KMN NTT) and 1470-1476 (coset KNR INTT)), evaluate the closure once on the full 4n domain (ZS = rotate-by-rho, Range-expressible in natural layout), multiply by the rho-periodic xnMinusOneInverse vector — note divideByZH's multiplier is index%rho-periodic in natural order / constant-per-n-block in bitrev (prove.go:1305-1317), so it is 4 Range-scoped constant vecMuls — then one 4n KNR INTT replaces both the scatter and divideByZH's ToCanonical (1320). This kills the scatter, scalingVector (982-986, 1018-1028), shifters, and bp rescaling outright. Cost: VRAM = (12+2c)*4n*32B = 1.6GB at n=2^20 but 6.4GB at n=2^22, which together with resident MSM bases (~0.5GB) exceeds the dev box's 8GB RTX 3070 — so at the top target size the big-domain variant must stream/chunk, and the rho-loop variant (small buffers) re-inherits the scatter problem. This trade-off is THE central design tension for any numerator offload.

== 3. Measured CPU profile (dev box: i7-11800H 16T, 31GB RAM; harness = refCircuit from backend/plonk/plonk_test.go:305-317 sized to exact power-of-2 domains; profile window covers Prove() only, 2-5 iterations; categories via pprof -focus sums, disjoint roots) ==
Prove wall: 2^16: 0.465s | 2^18: 1.81s | 2^20: 8.6s | 2^22: 36.4s. Avg parallelism ~12x.
Sample shares (of total prover CPU samples):
- MSM (processChunkG1BatchAffine/partitionScalars/batchAddG1Affine/innerMsmG1): 2^16: 54.7% | 2^18: 47.6% | 2^20: 43.3% | 2^22: 38.1%
- FFT (all fr/fft.*, includes numerator + divideByZH FFTs): 2^16: 29.7% | 2^18: 37.0% | 2^20: 42.2% | 2^22: 47.6%
- computeNumerator subtree total: 20.9% | 23.7% | 25.0% | 27.3%
  - of which func5 = per-coset INTT/scale/NTT pipeline (prove.go:1035-1057): 12.7% | 15.0% | 16.9% | 18.7%
  - of which iop.Evaluate = the constraint closure proper (allConstraints + gate/ordering/local): 7.6% | 7.5% | 7.2% | 6.9%  <- THE CLOSURE IS A ~7% ITEM AT EVERY SIZE
  - batchInvert: 0.17-0.23%; bitrev-scatter+restore goroutines (func6/func7): ~1.9% at 2^20; divideByZH non-FFT part: ~0.25%
So: MSM-only Amdahl ceiling (MSM -> 0): 2.21x (2^16), 1.91x (2^18), 1.76x (2^20), 1.62x (2^22). MSM + numerator-FFTs: ~2.9x at 2^22. MSM + ALL FFT: ~7x at 2^22 (requires solving everything above). Closure-only offload ceiling: 1.08x.

== 4. Measured GPU/PCIe numbers (RTX 3070 Laptop 8GB, driver CUDA 12.2, icicle-gnark v3.2.2 CUDA backend from the nix store, calls pinned via RunOnDevice, pageable host memory — no pinned API exists; 30-rep averages) ==
H2D: 6.24-6.59 GB/s (336us @2MB ... 20.8ms @128MB). D2H: 5.12-6.16 GB/s (21.9ms @128MB).
vecMul (size n, sync): 2^16: 25us (launch floor) | 2^18: 52us | 2^20: 172us | 2^22: 701us. FromMontgomery: ~same.
NTT in-place size n: 2^16: 170us | 2^18: 552us | 2^20: 2.16ms | 2^22: 9.06ms.
(For scale: one CPU FFT_n at 2^20 inside the prover costs ~15-20ms wall across 16 threads.)

== 5. Transfer-cost model for the hybrid (NTTs on GPU, closure on host) — scoring 'PCIe eats the win' ==
Host-shuttle model (the question's model — polynomials live on host, each coset iteration ships 12+2c vectors down and up): traffic = rho*2*(12+2c)*n*32B = 96n*32B at c=0 = 3.22GB/proof at 2^20 (matches the question's ~100n ~ 3GB), 12.9GB at 2^22. At measured ~6.3GB/s: 0.51s at 2^20, 2.05s at 2^22. Candidate saving = func5 wall ~= share*wall = 1.45s (2^20), 6.8s (2^22); GPU NTT replacement cost = 96 NTTs + 48 scale-vecMuls ~= 0.22s (2^20) / 0.90s (2^22). Net: 2^20: 1.45 - (0.51+0.22) = +0.7s (~8% of proof); 2^22: 6.8 - (2.05+0.90) = +3.9s (~11%); 2^16: traffic 0.20GB = 32ms + 96*launch ~= vs func5 wall ~59ms — fully erased. So PCIe eats the win below ~2^18 but NOT at 2^20-2^22 — though the residual win is single-digit-% of the proof, against substantial complexity.
Device-resident refinement: the per-iteration INTT can restart from the device-resident Lagrange values produced by the previous iteration, so only the down-leg to the host closure is needed: 48n*32B = 1.61GB (0.25s) at 2^20, 6.4GB (1.0s) at 2^22, +4n result upload; VRAM 12n*32B = 384MB (2^20) / 1.5GB (2^22) — fits. Net win improves to ~0.98s (11%) at 2^20, ~4.9s (13%) at 2^22. This is the best-value second increment after MSM.
Full-device closure (everything in Sec. 2): kernel time is trivial (~40+3c vecops * 4 iterations ~= 160 launches ~= 28ms at 2^20) + ~7n/iteration index-vector uploads (224MB -> 35ms) + 6-12 Montgomery passes — the cost is engineering risk, not GPU time; the prize is bounded by the closure's 7% share plus eliminating the 48n down-leg.

== 6. The MSM-only case, concretely ==
MSM inventory per proof (all kzg.Commit/Open over n-size bases): commitToLRO 3 partial MSMs (prove.go:404-...; padding-trimmed per the commitToLRO comment 387-403), Z 1 (commitToPolyAndBlinding 530-540), H 3 (commitToQuotient at 615, shards from 685-715), BatchOpenSinglePoint 1 (827-834), ZShiftedOpening 1, + tiny blinding MSMs (order <=3, commitBlindingFactor 536) ~= 9 size-n G1 MSMs.
- Scalar traffic (bases resident): 9n*32B = 288MB -> 45ms at 2^20; 1.15GB -> 0.18s at 2^22 — 1-2% of the time being replaced (3.7s / 13.9s respectively). PCIe cannot eat this win.
- VRAM: KzgLagrange (n G1 affine, 64B) + Kzg (n+3) ~= 512MB at 2^22 bn254 — fits 8GB with the Groth16 PinToGPU pattern (pk.deviceInfo / PinnedG1Device, icicle.go:1493-1509; one-time 512MB upload ~80ms amortized across proofs). bw6-761 triples element sizes — still fits at 2^22 (~2.3GB) but tight with anything else resident.
- Expected end-to-end: even a conservative GPU MSM estimate (<=200ms per 2^22 MSM incl. launch, consistent with the existing Groth16-ICICLE integration's purpose) gives 9*0.2+0.2 ~= 2.0s vs 13.9s CPU => prover 36.4s -> ~24.5s ~= 1.5x at 2^22, approaching the 1.62x ceiling; ~1.7x at 2^20, ~2.1x at 2^16 (MSM share is HIGHER at small n, and MSM transfers are tiny — MSM-only is the only scope whose win grows as n shrinks).
Recommended scoping for design decision (a): Increment 1 = MSMs only (9 call sites, no Montgomery/layout/broadcast hazards beyond the solved Groth16 patterns) -> ~1.5-2x measured-ceiling. Increment 2 = computeNumerator's per-coset NTT pipeline with device-resident state (no closure changes, +11-13% at 2^20-2^22, 48n down-leg only). Increment 3 (likely not worth it) = full-device closure: bounded at ~7% + the down-leg, and carries every hazard in Sec. 2 — broadcast materialization, R^(k-1) bookkeeping, ZS rotation/layout conflict, mid-proof alpha vector, host batch-invert syncs.
Key file:line index: prove.go closures 869-886 (gate), 901-924 (ordering, degree-4 at 914/919), 926-934+379-385 (local/L1), 953-980 (allConstraints; blinding 962-973; alpha fold 978), batchApply FFT pipeline 1035-1057, scatter 1069-1076, batchInvert 1130-1141, divideByZH 1287-1324; alpha timing 542-550/586-596; ZS 602 + iop/polynomial.go:157; rho 936 + domains 236-251; vecops core/vec_ops.go:13-17+63-78; no-D2D runtime/memory.go:62-87; Range core/slice.go:59-118; NTT orderings core/ntt.go:21-26; Groth16 precedents icicle.go:100-125 (Den broadcast), 121+1452-1463 (one-standard-operand rule), 1416-1428+1470-1476 (coset NTT orderings), 1493-1509 (pinned bases); broken GetRootOfUnity ntt/ntt.go:40-45; RunOnDevice runtime/runtime.go:93-96.

gap_answers.question: Where does the per-device GPU global state live for the new plonk packages: nttDomainMaxByDevice, deviceProveMu, and the warm-up sync.Once are all package-level in each generated groth16 curve package and in the dispatch package — does the design hoist them into a shared internal package (touching generated groth16 code) or document process-level mutual exclusion?
gap_answers.answer:
SHORT ANSWER: No artifact in the repo decides this. There is no DESIGN.md yet (it is the not-yet-written Phase-2 deliverable; GPU_EXPERIMENT.md:40-41 lists it as the Phase-2 exit criterion, the file's status line says "Phase 0 in progress" at GPU_EXPERIMENT.md:3, and `git status` on philippe/gpu-experiment shows only flake.nix/flake.lock added — no plonk packages exist; `ls backend/accelerated/icicle/` contains only doc.go, groth16/, internal/, opts.go). GPU_EXPERIMENT.md never mentions nttDomainMaxByDevice, deviceProveMu, warm-up, mutexes, or the domain singleton — its only NTT-adjacent risk is the generic coset-semantics item at GPU_EXPERIMENT.md:63-65. So "hoist into a shared internal package" vs "document process-level mutual exclusion" is an OPEN decision the design phase must make. Everything below is the load-bearing evidence for making it.

== 1. Where the state lives today (exact lines) ==

Per-curve generated packages — the identical block appears in all four, generated from one template:
- /home/work/repositories/gnark/backend/accelerated/icicle/groth16/bn254/icicle.go:53-60 — package-level `var ( nttDomainMu sync.Mutex; nttDomainMaxByDevice = make(map[int32]uint64); deviceProveMu = make(map[int32]*sync.Mutex); deviceProveMuLock sync.Mutex )`. Also per-package `msmChunkCapOnce/msmChunkCap` (62-65) and `msmMaxWindowOnce/msmMaxWindow` (67-70) — more package-level Onces a plonk package would duplicate (these are harmless to duplicate: they cache env-derived ints, no device side effects).
- bn254/icicle.go:79-86 — `getDeviceProveMutex(deviceID int32)` lazily creates the per-device mutex under `deviceProveMuLock`.
- Same lines in the other three: backend/accelerated/icicle/groth16/bls12-377/icicle.go:55,58,96,134,141-144; bls12-381/icicle.go same lines; bw6-761/icicle.go same lines (verified by grep — all four are byte-identical for this block).
- All four files carry "Code generated by gnark DO NOT EDIT" (bn254/icicle.go:4) and are produced from /home/work/repositories/gnark/backend/accelerated/icicle/internal/generator/templates/groth16.icicle.go.tmpl (state block at template lines 48, 51-52; getDeviceProveMutex at 73-78; fft.Generator(2*...) at 89; requestedDomainSize at 127; tracker compare/update at 134-137; ReleaseDomain at 144; InitDomain at 156) by /home/work/repositories/gnark/backend/accelerated/icicle/internal/generator/main.go (`//go:generate go run main.go` at main.go:22; bavard entry maps groth16.icicle.go.tmpl → ../../groth16/<curve>/icicle.go). Touching the groth16 side correctly means editing this template and regenerating — note the project quality bar explicitly defers codegen-template work (GPU_EXPERIMENT.md:15-16), which is in direct tension with hoisting.

Dispatch package:
- /home/work/repositories/gnark/backend/accelerated/icicle/groth16/groth16_icicle.go:33 — `var onceWarmUpDevice sync.Once` (package-level in package `groth16`).
- groth16_icicle.go:38-72 — `warmUpDevice(config)`: inside the Once it runs LoadBackend(config.BackendLibs, true) or LoadBackendFromEnvOrDefault() (41-51), GetDeviceCount (52), then per device CreateDevice + RunOnDevice{CreateStream (61) → WarmUpDevice(stream) (65)}. The created stream is NEVER destroyed — each execution of this Once body leaks one stream per device. Called from Prove at groth16_icicle.go:84. A mirrored plonk dispatch package gets its own independent Once → second LoadBackend + second leaked stream set + second warm-up grab.

== 2. The C-level singleton is real, per-curve, per-device (icicle-gnark v3.2.2) ==

- /home/work/go/pkg/mod/github.com/ingonyama-zk/icicle-gnark/v3@v3.2.2/wrappers/golang/curves/bn254/ntt/ntt.go:47-59 — `InitDomain` → C `bn254_ntt_init_domain`; `ReleaseDomain()` takes NO arguments and returns no handle → C `bn254_ntt_release_domain()` (header curves/bn254/ntt/include/ntt.h:15-16). No handle = one domain singleton per field library. It is scoped to the *currently active device*: all calls run inside `RunOnDevice` which does LockOSThread + SetDevice (wrappers/golang/runtime/runtime.go:93-100), so the backend keeps one domain per (field library, device).
- Linkage: wrappers/golang/curves/bn254/main.go:3 — `#cgo LDFLAGS: -L/usr/local/lib -licicle_field_bn254 -licicle_curve_bn254 -lstdc++`. A plonk-bn254 package importing the same `.../curves/bn254/ntt` wrapper links the SAME libicicle_field_bn254 into the same process → same C domain singleton as groth16-bn254, but with a second, blind Go-side tracker. Cross-curve there is NO sharing (bls12377/main.go:3 links -licicle_field_bls12_377, etc.), so a shared tracker must be keyed per curve as well as per device — a map[curve]map[deviceID] or one shared package instantiated per curve.
- The warm-up/LoadBackend state, by contrast, is curve-INDEPENDENT (libicicle_device, runtime/main.go:3 `-licicle_device`), so exactly one process-wide Once is the right shape regardless of curve.
- WarmUpDevice's "half of free VRAM" grab confirmed: runtime/runtime.go:22-33 — GetAvailableMemory; MallocAsync(mem.Free/2, stream); FreeAsync. Transient, but on the shared 8 GB dev GPU a second warm-up Once firing while a proof holds device memory can OOM that proof. Whether icicle_load_backend_from_env_or_default (runtime/include/runtime.h:13-14) is idempotent is undocumented in the wrapper — duplicate invocation is at best wasted work, at worst double registration.

== 3. The internally inconsistent convention (confirmed, with mechanism) ==

- bn254/icicle.go:96 — `gen, err := fft.Generator(2 * pk.Domain.Cardinality)`: the root of unity actually passed to InitDomain (converted at 128-132 into `rouIcicle`, used at 163) has order 2n. So the C domain twiddle table supports NTTs up to size 2n. (This 2n root is needed because computeH does coset NTTs; the coset generator written into pk.CosetGenerator at 130 is this same 2n-order element.)
- bn254/icicle.go:134 — `requestedDomainSize := uint64(pk.Domain.Cardinality)` records n (not 2n) into nttDomainMaxByDevice at 144; the grow-check at 141-146 compares n against previously recorded n's. Internally self-consistent for groth16 alone (everything is uniformly off by the same 2x), but as an ABSOLUTE record of the C domain's order it is wrong by 2x. Any plonk tracker that compares "I need a domain of order 4n" against groth16's recorded value inherits a 2x error in both directions: (a) plonk reading groth16's record underestimates the existing domain and does a needless Release+Init (dangerous, see below); (b) groth16 reading a plonk record that stores true order 4n would skip a re-init it actually... (groth16's n-convention vs true-order convention can also make groth16 wrongly think the domain is large enough). Decision for the design: if any state is shared, the shared tracker must record the ORDER OF THE ROOT PASSED TO InitDomain (i.e., 2*Cardinality for groth16; 4n or whatever the plonk big domain order is), and the groth16 template line 127 (= generated icicle.go:134) must be fixed to match — another forced touch of generated code under the hoist option.
- Bonus inherited hazard the design must not copy: Prove acquires the per-device prove mutex at bn254/icicle.go:821-823 ("CRITICAL: Must be acquired BEFORE solver phase..."), but `pk.setupDevicePointers(&device)` — which can ReleaseDomain (148-157) under only nttDomainMu (138-139) — is called at line 803, BEFORE proveMu is taken. So even within groth16 alone, a second Prove with a larger pk can ReleaseDomain on a device while a first Prove (holding proveMu) is mid-NTT. The deviceProveMu comments (56-57: "prevents concurrent NTT domain access which causes witness corruption") describe an invariant the code does not actually enforce across PKs. Mirroring this structure into plonk widens an existing race rather than creating a new one.

== 4. The concrete decision space (for the design phase) ==

Option A — hoist into a shared internal package (e.g. backend/accelerated/icicle/internal/devicestate, or per-curve subpackages there), holding: (1) per-(curve,device) domain tracker recording true initialized order + the domain mutex, (2) per-device GPU prove mutex shared by groth16 and plonk, (3) one process-wide warm-up Once parameterized by Config. Costs: must edit groth16.icicle.go.tmpl (lines 48-78, 89, 127-167) and rerun the generator at backend/accelerated/icicle/internal/generator (main.go:22) to regenerate all 4 icicle.go files, plus move groth16_icicle.go:33-72 into the shared package; conflicts with the stated "codegen deferred" quality bar but is the only option that makes concurrent groth16+plonk proving on the same curve/device safe in one process. Note plonk packages CANNOT simply import the groth16 per-curve package's state: the symbols are unexported (lowercase, bn254/icicle.go:54-59), and exporting them also touches generated code — so reuse-by-import degenerates into the same template edit.

Option B — duplicate the state in plonk packages and document process-level mutual exclusion ("do not prove groth16-icicle and plonk-icicle concurrently in one process on the same curve+device"). Costs: zero groth16 changes (consistent with the working-experiment bar and with Phase-2 designer bias "strict consistency with the Groth16 pattern", GPU_EXPERIMENT.md:55-56); but it is unenforceable, the duplicated dispatch Once still leaks an extra stream per device (groth16_icicle.go:61) and performs an extra Free/2 VRAM grab (runtime.go:27) even in SEQUENTIAL mixed use, and the documented rule must also cover the setup-before-mutex window of section 3 (a plonk setupDevicePointers can fire during a groth16 proof even if Proves are serialized by the caller, because warm-up/setup happen inside Prove).

Middle option worth recording — hoist only the curve-independent pieces (warm-up Once into the existing non-generated backend/accelerated/icicle package next to opts.go — Config with DeviceID/Backend/BackendLibs/PinToGPU is already there, opts.go:10-15 — both dispatch packages call it; leave per-curve trackers duplicated and document same-curve mutual exclusion). This fixes the stream leak/double-LoadBackend with zero generated-code changes, shrinking the documented rule to "no concurrent groth16+plonk proving on the same curve and device," but leaves the witness-corruption hazard real for that documented case and leaves the n-vs-2n recording bug latent.

Cross-curve note: a groth16-bn254 proof and a plonk-bls12-377 proof in one process share NO C NTT state (separate field libraries) but DO share the device runtime — the per-device prove mutexes in different curve packages are already independent today (each curve package has its own deviceProveMu map), so the existing groth16 code already implicitly accepts cross-curve concurrency on one device; only the SAME-curve case is new with plonk.
