| bw6-761 | 48 | 377 | 96 | 192 | 288 | fr/element.go:40-42 (Limbs=6, Bits=377, Bytes=48), fp/element.go:39-41 (Limbs=12, Bytes=96); icicle bw6761/base_field.go:9 (BASE_LIMBS=24), scalar_field.go:16 (SCALAR_LIMBS=12) |

Plonk uses G1 MSMs only — no G2 work anywhere in the prover hot path (all commits/opens go through kzg G1: backend/plonk/bn254/prove.go:300, 438, 662, 681, 788, 827-834, 1267-1277), so G2 sizes are irrelevant to this budget (unlike Groth16).

Planning baseline for "free VRAM": 8192 MiB total; CUDA context + ICICLE backend cost ~300-400 MiB empirically (not in code; `icicle_runtime.GetAvailableMemory` at wrappers/golang/runtime/runtime.go:40-50 returns the live number). I budget against ~7.3 GiB usable and the code's own 0.7x safety factor (see section 5).

## 1. Pinned dual SRS — (2n+3) G1 points

Plonk setup slices exactly two G1 bases (backend/plonk/bn254/setup.go:126-127): `pk.Kzg.G1 = srs.Pk.G1[:vk.Size+3]` (canonical, n+3 points; +3 for the kzg.Open of the blinded poly, checked at setup.go:109-110) and `pk.KzgLagrange.G1 = srsLagrange.Pk.G1` (Lagrange, exactly n points, setup.go:114-117). The PinToGPU analog (template: groth16 icicle.go:185-261, which pins via `loadG1` = CopyToDevice + in-place AffineFromMontgomery, no extra staging buffer, icicle.go:319-331) therefore costs (2n+3)*A:

| n | bn254 (A=64) | bls12-377/381 (A=96) | bw6-761 (A=192) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2^16 | 8 MiB | 12 MiB | 24 MiB |
| 2^18 | 32 MiB | 48 MiB | 96 MiB |
| 2^20 | 128 MiB | 192 MiB | 384 MiB |
| 2^21 | 256 MiB | 384 MiB | 768 MiB |
| 2^22 | 512 MiB | 768 MiB | 1536 MiB |

(The 2^20 bn254 row reproduces the map's lone "128 MB" data point.) Per-MSM, only one of the two bases is touched: Lagrange base for the size-`offset<=n` wire/Z/BSB22 commits (prove.go:438 — note commitToLRO deliberately MSMs only `offset = nbPublic+nbConstraints` entries, prove.go:404-444), canonical base for h1/h2/h3 (prove.go:1267-1277), the two openings (prove.go:681, 827-834) and the linearized poly (prove.go:788). If bases are NOT pinned, each of the ~(7+c) size-n-class MSMs re-uploads n*A per call (bn254 n=2^22: 256 MiB per MSM over PCIe) — that is the case for pinning both.

## 2. Numerator offload — (12+2c) size-n scalar vectors + 4n cres

`s.x` is allocated with 13+2c slots (prove.go:231, ids at prove.go:44-59) but `id_ZS` is a ShallowClone of `id_Z` sharing the same coefficient array (prove.go:602), so there are 12+2c distinct n-element vectors (c = number of BSB22 commitments; c=0 for plain circuits). The numerator's result `cres` is domain1.Cardinality = 4n (prove.go:949, domain1 set to 4*sizeSystem at prove.go:250, 8n only when n<6, prove.go:247-248). Working vectors if the rho-pass structure is mirrored on device: `buf` n (prove.go:950), `twiddles0` n (prove.go:844), scalingVector/scalingVectorRev n each (prove.go:983-986, 1022-1027), precomputedDenominators + bufBatchInvert n each (prove.go:993-994 — these feed computeLagrangeOneOnCoset, host-side batch inversion, prove.go:1130+, and would likely stay on host).

Core device-resident bytes = (12+2c)*n*s + 4n*s = (16+2c)*n*s, plus ~2n*s for scaling/working vectors. At c=0:

| n | bn254/bls12-x (512n B core) | bw6-761 (768n B core) |
|---|---|---|
| 2^16 | 32 MiB | 48 MiB |
| 2^18 | 128 MiB | 192 MiB |
| 2^20 | 512 MiB | 768 MiB |
| 2^21 | 1024 MiB | 1536 MiB |
| 2^22 | 2048 MiB | 3072 MiB |

Each BSB22 commitment adds 2n*s (two more vectors). The 4n cres slice alone (which becomes h via in-place divideByZH, prove.go:609, and whose h1/h2/h3 are sub-slices of size n+2 / n+3, prove.go:689-724) is 4n*s = 512 MiB bn254 / 768 MiB bw6-761 at n=2^22.

## 3. divideByZH's 1/(X^n-1) — the DenDevice analog

Groth16's DenDevice is a full n-element device vector holding ONE repeated constant (icicle.go:100-125), consumed by an elementwise VecOp Mul (icicle.go:1461). Plonk's divideByZH (prove.go:1287-1324) multiplies the 4n bit-reversed cres by `xnMinusOneInverseLagrangeCoset[iRev % rho]` (prove.go:1312-1317) where only rho=4 distinct inverse values exist (prove.go:1327-1350). icicle-gnark v3.2.2 VecOps supports only elementwise Sub/Add/Mul on equal-length vectors (wrappers/golang/core/vec_ops.go:13-17) — no scalar-broadcast, no gather. Three options, costed:

(a) Full 4n-element device vector of the expanded values: 4n*s = 512 MiB bn254 / 768 MiB bw6 at 2^22 (the question's framing). Precomputable at setup (values depend only on the domains, prove.go:1327-1350).
(b) **Cheaper option the code structure permits**: in BitReverse layout over 4n, `iRev % rho` equals the bit-reversed top-2 bits of i, which is CONSTANT on each contiguous quarter [k*n,(k+1)*n). So 4 in-place VecOp Mul calls on contiguous n-element ranges against a single n-element constant vector (refilled 4x, or 4 resident n-vectors) suffice: n*s = 128 MiB (bn254) / 192 MiB (bw6) at 2^22, or 4n*s if all four are kept resident.
(c) Host-side pointwise pass (utils.Parallelize as today, prove.go:1312-1317): 0 device bytes, but forces a 4n*s download+upload round-trip unless the subsequent 4n coset-INTT (`a.ToCanonical(bigDomain)`, prove.go:1320) also runs on host.

## 4. ICICLE NTT-domain tables for size 4n

InitDomain sizes the table from the ORDER OF THE ROOT you pass, not an explicit size (ntt.cuh:452-470 squares until 1): groth16 passes `fft.Generator(2*cardinality)` (icicle.go:96); Plonk must pass a 4n-order root (domain1.Generator) since the quotient INTT is size 4n. Allocations (icicle/backend/cuda/src/ntt/ntt.cuh:474-477): `cudaMallocManaged((max_size+1)*sizeof(S))` external twiddles, plus tiny internal tables (6 + 5x64 elements, mixed_radix_ntt.cu:599-610). Fast-twiddles mode would add 4N more (ntt.cuh:481-496) but is OFF by default: gnark uses GetDefaultNTTInitDomainConfig() with Ext=nil (groth16 icicle.go:163; wrappers/golang/core/ntt.go:108-114) and cuda_ntt.cu:14-17 only enables it via the config extension. So domain cost = (4n+1)*s, one-time per device (grown/released via nttDomainMaxByDevice, icicle.go:134-168):

| n | bn254/bls12-x | bw6-761 |
|---|---|---|
| 2^20 | 128 MiB | 192 MiB |
| 2^21 | 256 MiB | 384 MiB |
| 2^22 | 512 MiB | 768 MiB |

(managed memory, so it can spill to host under pressure rather than hard-OOM, at a perf cost.)

**Hidden per-call cost — arbitrary coset**: Plonk's coset generator is FrMultiplicativeGen (vk.CosetShift, setup.go), which is NOT a power of the domain root, so it misses ICICLE's coset_index map (only powers of the primitive root are registered, ntt.cuh:500-510). Every coset (I)NTT then (ntt.cuh:686-704): computes `size` coset powers SERIALLY on the host CPU and cudaMallocAsyncs `size*sizeof(S)` on device, freed after the call (ntt.cuh:740). For the one 4n coset-INTT per proof (divideByZH's ToCanonical, prove.go:1320) at bn254 n=2^22 that is a 512 MiB transient + ~4M serial host field-muls. The rho-pass numerator structure itself needs only PLAIN size-n NTTs (coset folded into the explicit scaling vectors, prove.go:1035-1057), so this hits once per proof. Mitigation for the design: keep a resident 4n coset-power vector (another 4n*s) and do VecOp-mul + plain NTT instead. Also: NTT with host input/output allocates device buffers of input_size_bytes itself (ntt.cuh:672-684); mixed-radix runs in-place on d_output with no large temporaries (only twiddle tables; grep of mixed_radix_ntt.cu shows no other cudaMalloc).

## 5. MSM chunk working memory

The groth16 costing template (mirrored identically in bw6-761/icicle.go:458/589/720): chunks are capped at 2^18 elements hard (getConfiguredMSMChunkCap, icicle.go:577-584; "empirically verified stable" for large curves), window c <= 16 default (icicle.go:586-598, env ICICLE_MSM_MAX_WINDOW), and per-chunk memory is modeled in computeRequiredMSMMemory (icicle.go:731-781) — corroborated by the real CUDA allocations (cuda_msm.cuh:423-425 three uint32 index arrays of size m*nofBms + sort temp ~ a 4th, :499 scalars, :536 points, :578 buckets sizeof(P)*(nofBms*2^c + nofBms)):

- scalarsMem = s*m (icicle.go:758) — credited back if already on device (icicle.go:775-777)
- indicesMem = 16*m*nofBms, nofBms = ceil(fr.Bits/c) (icicle.go:759, 749)
- pointsMem = A*m (icicle.go:760) — credited back if pinned (icicle.go:772-774)
- bucketsMem = 4*P*2^c*nofBms (bucketFactor 4, icicle.go:765-766)
- everything compared against 0.7*free (icicle.go:779; chunkCountFromCap also uses 0.7*free/(s+A+128), icicle.go:555-575); free is re-read via GetAvailableMemory at EVERY MSM (icicle.go:474-477), so chunking auto-adapts to whatever is pinned. Minimum 4 chunks whenever scalars or bases come from host (icicle.go:537-540). When bucketsMem > 0.7*free the tuner lowers c: nextC = floor(log2(reduced/(3*P*nofBms))) (icicle.go:666-704).

Worst-case transient per chunk (m = min(msmSize, 2^18), c=16):

| curve | buckets (4*P*2^16*nofBms) | indices (16*m*nofBms, m=2^18) | total transient |
|---|---|---|---|
| bn254 (nofBms=16) | 384 MiB | 64 MiB | ~448 MiB |
| bls12-377/381 (16) | 576 MiB | 64 MiB | ~640 MiB |
| bw6-761 (nofBms=24) | 1728 MiB | 96 MiB | ~1824 MiB; auto-degrades: c=15 -> nofBms=26, buckets ~936 MiB; c=14 -> nofBms=27, ~486 MiB |

Plus, when scalars are not device-resident, a per-MSM n*s upload (bn254 2^22: 128 MiB, freed after). Plonk runs ~(7+c) size-n-class G1 MSMs per proof: 3 LRO (size offset<=n, prove.go:438), c BSB22 (size n, prove.go:300), Z (n, prove.go:662), h1/h2/h3 (n+2 each, or n+3/n+3/n+2 with StatisticalZK, prove.go:689-724, commits 1267-1277), ZShifted open (~n+2 from blindedZ of n+3 = n + order_blinding_Z+1, prove.go:679/1212-1220, orders at :72-75), linearized poly (n+3, prove.go:788/1366), batch open (~n+3, prove.go:827-834), plus 8 tiny (<=3-point) blinding MSMs (prove.go:1223-1235).

**Concurrency**: groth16 serializes ALL GPU ops through a per-device mutex (getDeviceProveMutex, icicle.go:77-86, "prevents concurrent NTT domain access"). If Plonk adopts it (it should — the prover's goroutine pipeline, chZ/chH channels, would otherwise overlap an MSM with a 4n NTT), the transient budget is max(MSM transient, NTT transient incl. the 4n*s arbitrary-coset alloc), NOT their sum.

## 6. WarmUpDevice

`WarmUpDevice` MallocAsyncs **Free/2** and immediately FreeAsyncs it (wrappers/golang/runtime/runtime.go:22-33) — it pre-expands the CUDA async memory pool. It runs once per device via sync.Once at the top of the first Prove, BEFORE any pinning (groth16_icicle.go:33-72, called at :84). On an empty 3070 that's a ~3.6 GiB transient; because it's freed and ordered before pinning, it contributes nothing to steady state and cannot OOM (it always asks for half of whatever is free).

## 7. Worked peak totals and verdicts (full-offload design: dual SRS pinned + 4n domain + device numerator + ZH option (b) + serialized GPU ops; c=0; +~0.35 GiB context)

Peak = SRS + domain(4n) + numerator(16n*s) + ZH(n*s) + max-transient(MSM buckets+indices vs 4n*s coset alloc) + context.

bn254: 2^20: ~1.6 GiB; 2^21: ~2.4 GiB; **2^22: ~3.9-4.4 GiB — fits comfortably**. 2^23 would be ~7.1+ GiB (and needs a 2^23 SRS): marginal, treat 2^22 as the bench cap.
bls12-377/381: 2^22: 768+512+2048+128+640+358 ~ **4.3-4.8 GiB — fits**.
bw6-761: 2^20: ~3.5 GiB fits (c=16 survives: 0.7*(7.3-1.75) GiB > 1.82 GiB); 2^21: 768+384+1536+96+1824+358 ~ **4.9 GiB — fits**; 2^22: residents alone = 1536+768+3072+192 = 5.57 GiB, leaving ~1.7 GiB free -> tuner drops c to 15 (0.7*1.7=1.2 GiB < 1.69 GiB buckets), total ~6.9-7.7 GiB -> **borderline-infeasible at full offload** (allocator fragmentation will likely kill it). Safe bw6 2^22 variants: host-side numerator (drops 3.07 GiB -> ~3.8 GiB peak, comfortable), or pin Lagrange SRS only (-768 MiB -> ~6.1 GiB, still tight), or cap c<=14 (buckets ~486 MiB -> ~6.4 GiB, ~0.9 GiB headroom).

**Design consequences**: (1) PinToGPU-analog for BOTH SRS bases is affordable by default for all curves up to 2^21, and up to 2^22 for bn254/bls12-x; make it size/curve-aware for bw6-761 at 2^22. (2) Numerator offload fits alongside dual pinned bases for bn254/bls12-x through 2^22 (2.0-2.8 GiB of resident scalars) but NOT for bw6-761 at 2^22. (3) Keep the existing 2^18 chunk cap and the GetAvailableMemory-driven adaptive c/chunking — it is what makes pinning and MSM coexist automatically. (4) divideByZH needs no 4n broadcast vector: 4 contiguous-quarter VecOps against an n-element constant vector (or fold into the host pass) — reserve 4n*s only if you also keep a resident coset-power table to avoid ICICLE's per-call arbitrary-coset alloc + serial host power loop. (5) Feasible benchmark range for GPU_EXPERIMENT.md success criterion 3 (GPU_EXPERIMENT.md:23, :45, :68): 2^16..2^22 for bn254/bls12-377/bls12-381; 2^16..2^21 for bw6-761 at full offload, 2^22 reachable with MSM-only offload.

gap_answers.question: What is the stage-wise correctness oracle and the randomness seam for CPU-vs-GPU comparison in the gnark Plonk ICICLE port?
gap_answers.answer:
# Stage-wise correctness oracle and randomness seam for CPU-vs-GPU Plonk comparison

## 1. Complete randomness inventory of the bn254 Plonk prover (the seam)

`grep -n SetRandom backend/plonk/bn254/prove.go` returns exactly five hits — these are the ONLY nondeterminism sources in the prover path:

1. **Blinding polynomials** — `getRandomPolynomial` at /home/work/repositories/gnark/backend/plonk/bn254/prove.go:1239-1253 (`a[i].SetRandom()` at :1247). Called from `initBlindingPolynomials` (prove.go:259-266) for `bp[id_Bl/id_Br/id_Bo/id_Bz]` with compile-time orders `order_blinding_L=1, R=1, O=1, Z=2` (prove.go:71-76). Note :1241-1243: passing `n==-1` cancels blinding (returns the zero polynomial) — but the orders are package constants, not options, so blinding cannot be disabled without editing/cloning the code.
2. **Quotient shard randomizers** — prove.go:239-242 in `newInstance`, gated on `opts.StatisticalZK` (default **false**; option `WithStatisticalZeroKnowledge` at /home/work/repositories/gnark/backend/backend.go:143-149). Consumed in `h1()/h2()/h3()` at prove.go:689-724. For Phase-3 comparison runs, simply not passing this option removes these two samples entirely.
3. **bsb22 hint blinding** — prove.go:293 and :296 inside `bsb22Hint` (prove.go:280-315), which is installed as a solver hint override in `initBSB22Commitments` (prove.go:268-277, `solver.OverrideHint` at :276). Only fires for circuits with Plonk commitments; the zkEVM target circuit must be checked, but plain test circuits won't hit it.

Everything else is deterministic given the witness, pk, and those samples:
- **All four Fiat–Shamir challenges** are pure functions of preceding commitments: `deriveRandomness` at /home/work/repositories/gnark/backend/plonk/bn254/verify.go:361-379 (binds point bytes, then `fs.ComputeChallenge`), `bindPublicData` at verify.go:315. gamma/beta derived at prove.go:509-519, alpha at prove.go:542-550 (invoked at :594), zeta at prove.go:552-555 (invoked at :619). The transcript hash is injectable via `WithProverChallengeHashFunction` (backend.go:103-112) but defaults to sha256 (backend.go:73) — already deterministic, no change needed.
- **KZG opening/batch-opening are deterministic.** `kzg.Open` (called at prove.go:681) and `kzg.BatchOpenSinglePoint` (prove.go:827-834) derive the folding challenge via `deriveGamma` using a fresh Fiat–Shamir transcript over the point/digests/claimed values (gnark-crypto kzg.go:559-571, fold at :534) — the lone `SetRandom` in gnark-crypto's kzg.go is at kzg.go:455 inside `BatchVerifyMultiPoints`, which is **verifier-side only** (/home/work/go/pkg/mod/github.com/consensys/gnark-crypto@v0.20.1/ecc/bn254/kzg/kzg.go:440-470).
- The constraint solver (prove.go:319-349) is deterministic apart from the bsb22 hint above; `completeQk` (prove.go:351+) is deterministic.

## 2. Why there is no injection point today

`fr.Element.SetRandom()` hardcodes `crypto/rand.Reader`: /home/work/go/pkg/mod/github.com/consensys/gnark-crypto@v0.20.1/ecc/bn254/fr/element.go:300 (signature `func (z *Element) SetRandom() (*Element, error)`, no reader param), with `io.ReadFull(rand.Reader, bytes[:k])` at element.go:323 (rejection sampling per the comment at :296-302; `MustSetRandom` at :343-345). `ProverConfig` (backend.go:59-65) carries only `SolverOpts, HashToFieldFn, ChallengeHash, KZGFoldingHash, StatisticalZK` — hash seams exist, randomness seams do not.

Precedent check: the existing Groth16 ICICLE port did NOT add a hook either — it copies `_r.SetRandom()/_s.SetRandom()` verbatim from /home/work/repositories/gnark/backend/groth16/bn254/prove.go:173-176 into /home/work/repositories/gnark/backend/accelerated/icicle/groth16/bn254/icicle.go:1038-1041. So the deterministic-randomness hook is genuinely new work for the Plonk clone, not something to mirror.

## 3. Proposed seam mechanism (for the cloned prover)

Since the ICICLE Plonk prover will be a per-curve clone (like icicle/groth16/bn254/icicle.go), the clone owns its `instance` struct (native version at prove.go:156-203, ctor `newInstance` at prove.go:205-257). Recommended design:

- Add a field to the cloned instance, e.g. `randElement func(domainTag string, i int) fr.Element` or `blindingSource io.Reader`-per-site, defaulting to `fr.Element.SetRandom` / `crypto/rand.Reader`. Populate it from an icicle-package prover option (the icicle package already has its own opts.go: /home/work/repositories/gnark/backend/accelerated/icicle/opts.go) or an exported test-only setter; do NOT touch the public `backend.ProverConfig`.
- Replace the five call sites in the clone: `getRandomPolynomial` must become a method on `instance` (or take the source as a parameter) since it is currently a free function (prove.go:1239); `quotientShardsRandomizers` in `newInstance` (:240-241); the two `SetRandom`s in `bsb22Hint` (:293, :296).
- **Load-bearing concurrency caveat:** `Prove` launches 9 goroutines concurrently with channel-based sync (prove.go:121-145; channels declared :190-198). `initBlindingPolynomials` runs on its own goroutine (:127), `quotientShardsRandomizers` is sampled synchronously in `newInstance` (:239-242), and `bsb22Hint` runs inside the solver goroutine. A single shared stateful `io.Reader` would be read in nondeterministic interleaved order — CPU and GPU runs would diverge even with identical seeds. The hook must be **domain-separated per call site** (e.g., HKDF/hash of `seed || tag` with tags like "bl","br","bo","bz","qsr0","qsr1","bsb22-<depth>-<slot>", deterministic per (tag,index) regardless of goroutine schedule). Map bytes to field elements with the same convention on both sides (e.g., `fr.Element.SetBytes` of a 32-byte hash; exact uniformity is irrelevant for a correctness oracle).
- **The CPU reference needs the same hook.** Two viable shapes: (a) the comparison test runs both provers from the icicle package, where the "CPU run" is the clone with GPU paths switched off via the existing build-tag/dispatch pattern (icicle/groth16 uses `//go:build icicle` — see groth16_icicle.go / groth16_noicicle.go / groth16_all.go in /home/work/repositories/gnark/backend/accelerated/icicle/) — zero changes to backend/plonk/bn254; or (b) patch the native prover too (invasive, not recommended). Option (a) means the clone should keep a pure-Go fallback for each replaced kernel, which is independently useful for bisecting MSM-vs-NTT bugs.

## 4. The stage-wise oracle: checkpoint list

With identical per-site randomness, every intermediate below is a bit-exact pure function of (witness, pk). Checkpoints in pipeline order, with the natural emission point (each value is final when its channel closes):

| # | Checkpoint | Where computed | Final at |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | blinding polys bp[0..3] coefficients | prove.go:259-266 | close(s.chbp) :264 |
| 2 | L,R,O Lagrange vectors (solver output) | prove.go:319-339 | before :344 |
| 3 | proof.LRO[0..2] | commitToLRO prove.go:404-489 (NOTE: this branch carries a custom reduced-MSM version, identity documented :387-403; `MultiExp` at :438/:457/:476, blinding via `commitBlindingFactor` :1223-1236) | close(s.chLRO) :347 |
| 4 | proof.Bsb22Commitments | prove.go:300 (kzg.Commit on KzgLagrange) | inside solver |
| 5 | gamma, beta | prove.go:509-519 | close(s.chGammaBeta) :521 |
| 6 | Z Lagrange vector + proof.Z | buildRatioCopyConstraint prove.go:635-667, commit via commitToPolyAndBlinding :530-540 at :662 | close(s.chZ) :664 |
| 7 | alpha | prove.go:548 | within computeQuotient :594 |
| 8 | numerator `cres` (LagrangeCoset, BitReverse) | computeNumerator prove.go:841-1123 (result wrapped :1119) | return of computeNumerator |
| 9 | h canonical coefficients | divideByZH prove.go:1287-1324 (ToCanonical(bigDomain) :1320) | :609 |
| 10 | h1/h2/h3 shards | prove.go:689-724 | call at :615 |
| 11 | proof.H[0..2] | commitToQuotient prove.go:1263-1284 | :615 |
| 12 | zeta | prove.go:553 | :619 |
| 13 | blindedZ + proof.ZShiftedOpening | openZ prove.go:670-687 (getBlindedCoefficients :1212-1220, kzg.Open :681) | close(s.chZOpening) :685 |
| 14 | linearizedPolynomial + its digest | computeLinearizedPolynomial prove.go:726-794 (digest kzg.Commit :788; innerComputeLinearizedPoly :1366+) | chLinearizedPolynomial |
| 15 | proof.BatchedProof | batchOpening prove.go:796-839 (BatchOpenSinglePoint :827, deterministic given kzgFoldingHash + ZShiftedOpening.ClaimedValue :833) | end |

Oracle semantics: run CPU and GPU with the same seed; compare checkpoints in order; the first divergence localizes to a single stage (one MSM batch or one NTT block). Challenges 5/7/12 are free integrity checks — they hash the preceding commitments, so a challenge mismatch == a commitment byte mismatch. Suggested mechanism: an optional `onStageCheckpoint func(name string, payload []byte)` field on the cloned instance (nil in production), invoked at the channel-close points above; serialize fr vectors with `fr.Vector.WriteTo`-style raw bytes and points with `RawBytes()` so comparisons are byte-exact and Montgomery-form bugs are caught (this is exactly where ICICLE `FromMontgomery` mistakes will surface).

## 5. IsDifferent / marshal-test decision (the flagged open item)

- groth16 has `IsDifferent` on both pk and vk: /home/work/repositories/gnark/backend/groth16/bn254/setup.go:599-634 (vk :601-612, pk :616-634; per-curve copies, e.g. bls12-377 setup.go:599/616), declared in the interfaces at /home/work/repositories/gnark/backend/groth16/groth16.go:76-77 and :110. Its real purpose is asserting two keys ARE different (random-sampling check); the icicle marshal test uses it inverted — `if iciPK.IsDifferent(nativePK) { t.Error(...) }` after a WriteTo/ReadFrom round trip: /home/work/repositories/gnark/backend/accelerated/icicle/groth16/marshal_test.go:41-43 and :72-74.
